mishnayos.stIntro: The early commentaries ask why this chapter, which discusses details of the halakhot of found items, precedes the second chapter, which discusses the fundamental halakhot of found items. Tosafot explain that as tractate Bava Metzia follows tractate Bava Kamma, the halakhot of found items are elucidated in this chapter as a continuation of the topics discussed in the last chapter of Bava Kamma, which discussed the division of items between litigants by means of an oath, which is also the ruling in the mishna here (see Shita Mekubbetzet). The Rosh explains that because there is a suspicion of theft in this case, these matters are juxtaposed with the halakhot of theft, which are described at length in Bava Kamma.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna is an excerpt from a halakhic midrash concerning lost items, based on the verse: “You shall not see your brother’s ox or his sheep wandering, and disregard them; you shall return them to your brother…And so shall you do with his donkey; and so shall you do with his garment; and so shall you do with every lost item of your brother, which shall be lost from him, and you have found it; you may not disregard it” (Deuteronomy 22:1, 3).

mishnayos.summary: How long must a finder keep announcing? Rabbi Meir says until his neighbors know of it; Rabbi Yehuda says through three Yamim Tovim and seven days after the last one.

chunks.en: And until when must he announce?
chunks.st: And until when is one who finds a lost item obligated to proclaim his find? He is obligated to do so

chunks.en: Until his neighbors know about it.
chunks.st: until the moment that the neighbors will know of its existence;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: He is obligated to proclaim his find for

chunks.en: Three Yamim Tovim,
chunks.explain: Pesach, Shavuos and Sukkos, when everyone came to Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: three pilgrimage Festivals

chunks.en: and seven days after the last Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and for seven days after the last of the three pilgrimage Festivals,

chunks.en: so that the owner can go home, three days,
chunks.st: so that its owner will have time to go to his home, a trip lasting up to three days, and ascertain that he in fact lost the item,

chunks.en: and come back, three days,
chunks.st: and he will return to Jerusalem, a trip lasting up to three days,

chunks.en: and announce his loss for one day.
chunks.st: and proclaim his loss for one day.

mishnayos.summary: A finder gives a lost thing back only to someone who tells its signs, and not to a cheater. The mishnah teaches what to do with a found animal, and what happens with money from selling it.

chunks.he: אָמַר אֶת הָאֲבֵדָה וְלֹא אָמַר סִימָנֶיהָ,
chunks.en: If someone said what the lost thing was but did not say its signs,
chunks.st: If a claimant accurately stated what type of item the lost item that was found by another is, but did not state, i.e., describe, its distinguishing marks,

chunks.en: he should not give it to him.
chunks.st: the finder shall not give it to him.

chunks.he: וְהָרַמַּאי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר סִימָנֶיהָ,
chunks.en: And a cheater, even though he said its signs,
chunks.st: And in the case of a swindler, even though he stated its distinguishing marks,

chunks.en: he should not give it to him,
chunks.st: the finder shall not give the lost item to him,

chunks.en: as it says in the Torah,
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And if your brother be not near you, and you know him not, then you shall bring it into your house, and it shall be with you

chunks.en: "Until your brother asks for it."
chunks.st: until your brother claims [derosh] it [oto],
chunks.stMore: and you shall return it to him” (Deuteronomy 22:2). Would it enter your mind that the finder would give it to him before he claims it? How can the finder return it if he does not know the identity of the owner? Rather, the verb derosh is not referring to the claim of the owner; it is referring to the scrutiny performed by the finder.

chunks.en: This means: until you check your brother
chunks.st: You shall not return the lost item until you scrutinize [shetidrosh] your brother to determine

chunks.he: אִם רַמַּאי הוּא אִם אֵינוֹ רַמָּאי.
chunks.en: whether he is a cheater or not a cheater.
chunks.st: whether he, the claimant, is a swindler or whether he is not a swindler.

chunks.en: Any animal that works and eats
chunks.st: If one finds any living being that works and generates enough revenue to cover the costs of the food that it eats, it

chunks.en: should work and eat.
chunks.explain: Its work pays for its food.
chunks.st: shall work and eat while in the finder’s possession.

chunks.en: But an animal that does not work and only eats
chunks.st: And any living being that does not work but it does eat

chunks.en: should be sold,
chunks.st: shall be sold,

chunks.en: as it says, "And you shall return it to him":
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Then you shall bring it into your house, and it shall be with you until your brother claims it, and you shall return it to him” (Deuteronomy 22:2),

chunks.en: see how you can give it back to him.
chunks.explain: Feeding it too long would eat up all its value.
chunks.st: indicating that the finder must see how best to return it to him.
chunks.stMore: Since the owner must repay the finder for his expenditures, if feeding the animal costs more than its value, the finder’s keep-ing the animal in his possession will prevent the owner from recovering it.

chunks.en: What happens with the money?
chunks.st: What shall be done with the money received from the sale of the animal?

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says: The finder

chunks.en: He may use it.
chunks.st: may use it;

chunks.en: So if it gets lost, he must pay it back.
chunks.st: therefore, if the money is lost, he is liable to pay restitution for it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: He may not use it.
chunks.st: He may not use the money;

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן:
chunks.en: So if it gets lost, he does not have to pay it back.
chunks.st: therefore, if it is lost, he is not liable to pay restitution for it.

mishnayos.summary: A finder must take care of what he found: he airs out sefarim and clothes, and uses metal vessels a little so they do not spoil. He does not need to pick up things that are beneath his honor to carry.

chunks.en: If he found sefarim,
chunks.st: If one found scrolls,

chunks.en: he reads them once every thirty days.
chunks.explain: Opening them lets in air so they do not get moldy.
chunks.st: he reads them once in thirty days in order to ventilate them and prevent mold.

chunks.en: And if he does not know how to read, he rolls them open and closed.
chunks.st: And if he does not know how to read, he rolls and unrolls them in order to ventilate them.

chunks.en: But he should not learn something new from them,
chunks.st: But he shall not study passages in them for the first time,
chunks.stMore: as he would leave the scroll exposed to the air for a lengthy period, thereby causing damage.

chunks.en: and another person should not read with him.
chunks.st: And another person shall not read the scroll with him,
chunks.stMore: as each might pull it closer to improve his vantage point, which could cause the scroll to tear.

chunks.en: If he found a garment,
chunks.st: If one found a garment,

chunks.en: he shakes it out once every thirty days,
chunks.st: he shakes it once in thirty days,

chunks.en: and spreads it out for its own good,
chunks.st: and he spreads it out for its sake, to ventilate it,

chunks.en: but not to look fancy himself.
chunks.st: but he may not use it as a decoration for his own prestige.

chunks.en: Silver vessels and copper vessels
chunks.st: If one found silver vessels or copper vessels,

chunks.en: he uses for their own good,
chunks.st: he may use them for their own sake to prevent tarnish and rust,

chunks.en: but not so much that he wears them out.
chunks.st: but he may not use them to the extent that he will erode them.

chunks.en: Gold vessels and glass vessels
chunks.st: If he finds gold vessels or glass vessels, which are not ruined by neglect,

chunks.he: לֹא יִגַּע בָּהֶן עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ.
chunks.en: he should not touch until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.st: he may not touch them until Elijah will come and identify the owner.

chunks.en: If he found a sack or a basket,
chunks.st: If a person found a sack or a basket

chunks.en: or anything he would not usually carry,
chunks.st: or any other item that it is not his typical manner to take and carry because it is beneath his dignity,

chunks.en: he does not have to take it.
chunks.st: he shall not take it, as one need not demean himself in order to return a lost item.

mishnayos.summary: An animal is lost only when it looks lost, and one must return it even many times. If returning it costs the finder his work, he gets paid like an idle worker, unless he made a condition before beis din.

chunks.en: What counts as a lost thing?
chunks.st: Which is the item that is considered lost property?

chunks.he: מָצָא חֲמוֹר אוֹ פָרָה רוֹעִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ,
chunks.en: If he found a donkey or a cow eating grass on the road,
chunks.st: If one found a donkey or a cow grazing on the path,

chunks.en: that is not a lost thing.
chunks.explain: The owners are probably close by.
chunks.st: that is not lost property,
chunks.stMore: as presumably the owners are nearby and are aware of the animals’ whereabouts.

chunks.en: A donkey with its saddle and bags flipped over,
chunks.st: If one found a donkey with its accoutrements overturned,

chunks.en: a cow running between the vineyards,
chunks.st: or a cow that ran through the vineyards,

chunks.en: that is a lost thing.
chunks.st: that is lost property.

chunks.en: If he returned it and it ran away,
chunks.st: In a case where one returned the lost animal and it fled, and he again

chunks.en: returned it and it ran away,
chunks.st: returned it and it fled,

chunks.en: even four or five times,
chunks.st: even if this scenario repeats itself four or five times,

chunks.en: he must return it,
chunks.st: he is obligated to return it each time,

chunks.en: as it says, "You shall surely return them."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “You shall not see your brother’s ox or his sheep wandering and disregard them; you shall return them to your brother” (Deuteronomy 22:1).

chunks.en: If he stopped work that would have earned a sela,
chunks.explain: A sela is a silver coin.
chunks.st: If in the course of tending to and returning the lost item, the finder was idle from labor that would have earned him a sela,

chunks.he: לֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ תֶּן לִי סֶלַע,
chunks.en: he cannot say to the owner, "Give me a sela."
chunks.st: he shall not say to the owner of the item: Give me a sela to compensate me for my lost income.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא נוֹתֵן לוֹ שְׂכָרוֹ כְּפוֹעֵל בָּטֵל.
chunks.en: Instead, the owner pays him like a worker who sits idle.
chunks.explain: A worker would take less pay to rest instead.
chunks.st: Rather, the owner gives him his wage as if he were a laborer, a payment that is considerably smaller.

chunks.en: If there is a beis din there,
chunks.st: If there are three men there who can convene as a court,

chunks.en: he makes a condition in front of beis din.
chunks.explain: He says he will return it only for full pay.
chunks.st: he may stipulate before the court
chunks.stMore: that he will undertake to return the item provided that he receives full compensation for lost income.

chunks.en: If there is no beis din there,
chunks.st: If there is no court there

chunks.en: in front of whom can he make a condition?
chunks.st: before whom can he stipulate his condition,

chunks.en: His own comes first.
chunks.st: his financial interests take precedence and he need not return the lost item.

mishnayos.summary: The mishnah teaches when a found animal must be returned, that a father cannot tell his son to break a mitzvah, and the mitzvah to help unload and load an animal under its burden.

chunks.en: If he found it in a stable,
chunks.st: If one found an animal in a stable belonging to its owner,

chunks.en: he does not have to return it.
chunks.st: he is not obligated to return it to its owner.

chunks.en: In a public place,
chunks.st: If he found it in a public area,

chunks.en: he must return it.
chunks.st: he is obligated to return it.

chunks.en: And if it was in a graveyard,
chunks.st: And if the animal was lost in a graveyard and a priest found it,

chunks.en: a Kohen may not become tamei for it.
chunks.explain: A Kohen may not go into a graveyard.
chunks.st: he may not become impure to return it.

chunks.en: If his father told him,
chunks.st: If his father said to him:

chunks.en: "Become tamei," or told him,
chunks.st: Become impure; or in a case where one was obligated to return the animal and his father said to him:

chunks.en: "Do not return it,"
chunks.st: Do not return it,

chunks.en: he should not listen to him.
chunks.explain: We may not break the Torah even to honor a father.
chunks.st: he may not listen to his father, as one may not violate Torah law to honor his father.

chunks.en: If he unloaded and loaded,
chunks.st: If one unloaded a burden from an animal collapsing under its weight and then later loaded it onto the animal,

chunks.en: unloaded and loaded,
chunks.st: and later unloaded and loaded it again,

chunks.en: even four or five times,
chunks.st: even if this scenario repeats itself four or five times,

chunks.en: he must keep helping, as it says, "You shall surely help."
chunks.st: he is obligated to continue unloading and loading, as it is stated: “If you see the donkey of him that hates you collapsed under its burden, you shall forgo passing him by; you shall release it [azov ta’azov]
chunks.stMore: with him” (Exodus 23:5). It is derived from the verse that one is obligated to perform the action as needed, even several times.

chunks.en: If the owner went and sat down and said,
chunks.st: If the owner went, and sat, and said to a passerby:

chunks.en: "Since the mitzvah is on you,
chunks.st: Since there is a mitzva incumbent upon you to unload the burden,

chunks.en: if you want to unload, unload,"
chunks.st: if it is your wish to unload the burden, unload it,

chunks.en: the passerby does not have to, as it says, "with him."
chunks.explain: The owner must help too.
chunks.st: in such a case the passerby is exempt, as it is stated: “You shall release it with him,” with the owner of the animal.

chunks.he: אִם הָיָה זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה, חַיָּב.
chunks.en: If the owner was old or sick, the passerby must help.
chunks.st: If the failure of the owner to participate in unloading the burden was due to the fact he was old or infirm, the passerby is obligated to unload the burden alone.

chunks.en: It is a mitzvah from the Torah to unload,
chunks.st: There is a mitzva by Torah law to unload a burden,

chunks.en: but not to load.
chunks.st: but there is no mitzva to load it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Also to load.
chunks.st: There is even a mitzva to load the burden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

chunks.he: אִם הָיָה עָלָיו יָתֵר עַל מַשָּׂאוֹ,
chunks.en: If it had more on it than its proper load,
chunks.st: If there was a burden upon the animal greater than its typical burden,

chunks.en: he does not have to help,
chunks.st: one need not attend to it,

chunks.en: as it says, "under its load,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Under its burden,” i.e., the obligation is with regard to

chunks.en: a load that it is able to carry.
chunks.st: a burden that the animal can bear.

mishnayos.summary: When one can return only one lost thing, his own comes first, and his rebbi's comes before his father's, because his rebbi brings him to Olam Haba. If his father is a talmid chacham, his father comes first.

chunks.en: His own lost thing and his father's lost thing:
chunks.st: If one finds his lost item and his father’s lost item,

chunks.en: his own lost thing comes first.
chunks.st: tending to his own lost item takes precedence.

chunks.en: His own lost thing and his rebbi's lost thing:
chunks.st: Similarly, if one finds his lost item and his teacher’s lost item,

chunks.en: his own comes first.
chunks.st: tending to his own lost item takes precedence.

chunks.en: His father's lost thing and his rebbi's lost thing:
chunks.st: If one finds his father’s lost item and his teacher’s lost item,

chunks.en: his rebbi's comes first,
chunks.st: tending to his teacher’s lost item takes precedence,

chunks.en: because his father brought him into this world,
chunks.st: as his father brought him into this world,

chunks.en: but his rebbi, who taught him Torah wisdom, brings him
chunks.st: and his teacher, who taught him the wisdom of Torah,

chunks.en: to the life of Olam Haba.
chunks.st: brings him to life in the World-to-Come.

chunks.en: But if his father is a talmid chacham,
chunks.st: And if his father is a Torah scholar, then

chunks.en: his father's comes first.
chunks.st: his father’s lost item takes precedence.

chunks.en: If his father and his rebbi were carrying loads,
chunks.st: If his father and his teacher were each carrying a burden and he wants to assist them in putting down their burdens, he first

chunks.en: he puts down his rebbi's first,
chunks.st: places his teacher’s burden down

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵנִיחַ אֶת שֶׁל אָבִיו.
chunks.en: and after that he puts down his father's.
chunks.st: and thereafter places his father’s burden down.

chunks.en: If his father and his rebbi were captured,
chunks.st: If his father and his teacher were in captivity, he first

chunks.en: he frees his rebbi first,
chunks.explain: Redeem means to pay to set someone free.
chunks.st: redeems his teacher

chunks.en: and after that he frees his father.
chunks.st: and thereafter redeems his father.

chunks.en: But if his father is a talmid chacham,
chunks.st: And if his father is a Torah scholar, he first

chunks.en: he frees his father first,
chunks.st: redeems his father

chunks.en: and after that he frees his rebbi.
chunks.st: and thereafter redeems his teacher.

mishnayos.summary: A shomer who was not paid lost the animal or things he was watching. If he paid the owner instead of swearing, he gets the thief's extra payments; if he swore instead, the owner gets them.

chunks.he: הַמַּפְקִיד אֵצֶל חֲבֵרוֹ בְּהֵמָה אוֹ כֵלִים,
chunks.en: If someone left an animal or vessels with his friend to watch,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits an animal or vessels with another, who is acting as an unpaid bailee,

chunks.en: and they were stolen or lost,
chunks.st: and they were stolen or they were lost, and

chunks.en: and the watchman paid and did not want to swear,
chunks.st: the bailee paid the owner the value of the deposit, and did not wish to take an oath
chunks.stMore: that he did not misappropriate the item and that he was not negligent in safeguarding it, that will effect who keeps the deposit if it is found or returned.

chunks.he: שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם נִשְׁבָּע וְיוֹצֵא,
chunks.en: even though the Sages said a free watchman swears and goes free,
chunks.explain: He swears he did not take it and was not careless.
chunks.st: The bailee may also choose to take the oath, as the Sages said: An unpaid bailee takes an oath, and he is thereby released from the liability to pay the owner.

chunks.en: if the thief is found,
chunks.st: If the thief is later found,

chunks.en: he pays double.
chunks.explain: A thief must pay back twice what he stole.
chunks.st: the thief pays the double payment.

chunks.en: If he slaughtered or sold it,
chunks.st: If the deposited item was a sheep or an ox and the thief slaughtered or sold it,

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.explain: Four times for a sheep, five times for an ox.
chunks.st: he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

chunks.en: To whom does he pay?
chunks.st: To whom does the thief pay?

chunks.en: To the one who had the deposit with him.
chunks.explain: The watchman paid, so he now owns it.
chunks.st: He gives the payment to the one who had the deposit in his
chunks.stMore: possession when it was stolen, i.e., the bailee. When the bailee paid the owner for the stolen item, the owner granted the rights to the item to the bailee. Therefore, the bailee is entitled to any payment the thief presents for the item, be it compensation for the item’s value or a fine.

chunks.en: If the watchman swore and did not want to pay,
chunks.st: In the case of a bailee who took an oath and did not wish to pay,

chunks.en: if the thief is found,
chunks.st: if the thief is then found

chunks.en: he pays double.
chunks.st: and required to pay the double payment,

chunks.en: If he slaughtered or sold it,
chunks.st: or if he slaughtered or sold the animal

chunks.en: he pays four or five times.
chunks.st: and is required to pay the fourfold or fivefold payment,

chunks.en: To whom does he pay?
chunks.st: to whom does the thief pay?

chunks.en: To the owner of the deposit.
chunks.st: He gives the payment to the owner of the deposit, not the bailee.

mishnayos.summary: Someone rented a cow and lent it to another person, and it died a normal death. The Tanna Kamma says the renter swears and the borrower pays him; Rabbi Yosei says the money goes back to the cow's owner.

chunks.en: If someone rents a cow from his friend and lends it to another person,
chunks.st: In the case of one who rents a cow from another, and this renter then lends it to another person,

chunks.en: and it died the normal way,
chunks.st: and the cow dies in its typical manner, i.e., of natural causes, in the possession of the borrower,

chunks.en: the renter swears that it died the normal way,
chunks.explain: A renter does not pay when an animal dies by itself.
chunks.st: the renter takes an oath to the owner of the cow that the cow died in its typical manner,

chunks.en: and the borrower pays the renter.
chunks.explain: A borrower pays even when it dies by itself.
chunks.st: and the borrower pays the renter
chunks.stMore: for the cow that he borrowed. A renter is exempt in a case of damage due to circumstances beyond his control, including death, but a borrower is liable to compensate the owner even for damage due to circumstances beyond his control.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: How can that one do business
chunks.st: How does the other party, i.e., the renter, do business with

chunks.en: with his friend's cow?
chunks.st: and profit from another’s cow?

chunks.en: Rather, the cow's value goes back to its owner.
chunks.st: Rather, the value of the cow should be returned to the owner.
chunks.stMore: The renter need not take an oath, but the borrower must compensate the owner of the cow.

mishnayos.summary: A man says he took money from one of two people, or was given money by one of their fathers, but does not know which one. He must pay each of them the full amount.

chunks.en: If he said to two people,
chunks.st: If one said to two people:

chunks.en: "I stole 100 zuz from one of you,
chunks.st: I robbed one of you of one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and I do not know which of you,"
chunks.st: but I do not know from which of you I took the money,

chunks.en: or, "The father of one of you
chunks.st: or if one said to two people: The father of one of you

chunks.en: left 100 zuz with me,
chunks.st: deposited one hundred dinars with me,

chunks.en: and I do not know which one he is,"
chunks.st: but I do not know the father of which of you he is,

chunks.en: he gives 100 zuz to this one and 100 zuz to that one,
chunks.st: then he gives one hundred dinars to this person and one hundred dinars to that person.

chunks.en: because he admitted it by himself.
chunks.st: This is because there is no way to determine which of them is entitled to the money, and he admitted his obligation at his own initiative.

mishnayos.summary: Two people left money with one person; each says the bigger amount was his. The Tanna Kamma gives each the smaller amount and puts the rest away until Eliyahu comes; Rabbi Yosei says to put it all away so the cheater loses.

chunks.en: Two people left money with one person,
chunks.st: In the case of two people who deposited money with one person,

chunks.en: this one 100 zuz and that one 200,
chunks.st: and this one deposited one hundred dinars and that one deposited two hundred dinars, and when they come to collect their deposit,

chunks.en: this one says, "Mine was 200,"
chunks.st: this one says: My deposit was two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and that one says, "Mine was 200."
chunks.st: and that one says: My deposit was two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: He gives 100 zuz to this one and 100 zuz to that one,
chunks.st: the bailee gives one hundred dinars to this one and one hundred dinars to that one.

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁאָר יְהֵא מֻנָּח עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ.
chunks.en: and the rest stays put until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.st: And the rest of the money, i.e., the contested one hundred dinars, will be placed in a safe place until Elijah comes and prophetically determines the truth.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.explain: Then the cheater may admit the truth.
chunks.st: until Elijah comes. As
chunks.stMore: his fraud will cause him to lose even the one hundred dinars that he deposited, perhaps he will be discouraged from making a fraudulent claim.

mishnayos.summary: Two people left two vessels, a cheap one and an expensive one, and each says the expensive one is his. Each gets the cheap one's value and the rest waits for Eliyahu; Rabbi Yosei says to put it all away.

chunks.en: And the same with two vessels,
chunks.st: And likewise, if two people deposited two vessels,

chunks.en: one worth 100 zuz
chunks.st: one worth one hundred dinars

chunks.en: and one worth 1,000 zuz.
chunks.st: and one worth one thousand dinars,

chunks.en: This one says, "The nice one is mine,"
chunks.st: and this one says: The expensive vessel is mine,

chunks.en: and that one says, "The nice one is mine."
chunks.st: and that one says: The expensive vessel is mine,

chunks.en: He gives the small one to one of them,
chunks.st: the bailee gives the small vessel to one of them,

chunks.he: וּמִתּוֹךְ הַגָּדוֹל נוֹתֵן דְּמֵי קָטָן לַשֵּׁנִי,
chunks.en: and from the big one he gives the small one's value to the other,
chunks.explain: He sells the big one to get the money.
chunks.st: and from the proceeds of the sale of the large vessel he gives the value of the small vessel to the other,

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁאָר יְהֵא מֻנָּח עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ.
chunks.en: and the rest stays put until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.st: and the rest of the money is placed in a safe place until Elijah comes.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: If so, what did the cheater lose?
chunks.st: If so, what did the swindler lose?

chunks.st: Rather, the entire deposit, i.e., both vessels,

chunks.en: until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.st: are placed in a safe place until Elijah comes or one of them admits his deceit.

mishnayos.summary: If someone left fruit with a watchman, the watchman may not touch it even if it is spoiling. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says he sells it in front of beis din, like returning a lost thing.

chunks.en: If someone leaves fruit with his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits produce with another,

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ הֵן אֲבוּדִין לֹא יִגַּע בָּהֶן.
chunks.en: even if it is going to waste, he should not touch it.
chunks.explain: It is not his.
chunks.st: even if it is lost due to spoilage or vermin, the bailee may not touch it, as it is not his.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: he sells it in front of beis din,
chunks.st: He sells it before the court,

chunks.en: because it is like returning a lost thing to its owner.
chunks.st: as by doing so he is like one returning a lost item to the owner,
chunks.stMore: since through its sale he prevents the owner from losing the value of his produce.

mishnayos.summary: When a watchman gives back fruit, he may take off a set amount that fruit normally shrinks. The Sages argue about how much and for how big a pile.

chunks.en: If someone leaves fruit with his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits produce with another, and the bailee provides him with different produce in return,

chunks.en: the watchman may take off the amount it shrinks.
chunks.explain: Stored fruit dries up and mice eat some.
chunks.st: that bailee deducts from the produce that he returns an amount equal to the standard decrease of the produce. The decrease is calculated according to this formula:

chunks.en: For wheat and rice,
chunks.st: For wheat and for rice,

chunks.en: nine half-kav for each kor.
chunks.explain: A kav and a kor are measures; a kor is 180 kav.
chunks.st: he deducts nine half-kav per kor, which is 180 kav;

chunks.en: For barley and millet,
chunks.st: for barley and millet,

chunks.en: nine kav for each kor.
chunks.st: he deducts nine kav per kor;

chunks.en: For spelt and flax seed,
chunks.st: for spelt and flaxseed,

chunks.en: three se'ah for each kor.
chunks.st: he deducts three se’a, which total eighteen kav, per kor.

chunks.en: It all goes by the amount,
chunks.st: The entire calculation is according to the measure,

chunks.en: it all goes by the time.
chunks.explain: This is the amount for one year.
chunks.st: and the entire calculation is according to the time
chunks.stMore: elapsed. This is the amount of produce that the bailee deducts per one kor of produce over the course of one year.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said:

chunks.en: "Why should the mice care?
chunks.st: And what do the mice care how much produce the bailee is safeguarding?

chunks.he: וַהֲלֹא אוֹכְלוֹת בֵּין מֵהַרְבֵּה וּבֵין מִקִּמְעָא.
chunks.en: Don't they eat the same from a lot or from a little?
chunks.st: Don’t they eat the same amount whether it is from much produce and whether it is from little produce?

chunks.en: Rather, he takes off the shrinking
chunks.st: Rather, he deducts an amount equal to the standard decrease

chunks.en: only for one kor."
chunks.st: of just one kor of produce.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If it was a big amount,
chunks.st: If the deposit was a large measure,

chunks.en: he does not take off anything,
chunks.st: the bailee does not deduct the decrease from it,

chunks.en: because it grows.
chunks.explain: Fruit can swell, so it evens out.
chunks.st: due to the fact that for different reasons it increases.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, he returns the measure of produce that was deposited with him, because the increase offsets the decrease.

mishnayos.summary: When giving back wine or oil, a watchman may take off a set amount for what soaks into the barrel and what sinks to the bottom. Rabbi Yehuda says a buyer of clear oil also accepts a set amount of sediment.

chunks.en: He may take off one sixth for wine.
chunks.explain: Wine soaks into the barrel and dries up.
chunks.st: When the bailee returns liquids that were deposited with him, he deducts one-sixth of the amount for wine,
chunks.stMore: to offset the decrease in volume due to absorption into the cask and evaporation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says, one fifth.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: He deducts one-fifth.

chunks.he: יוֹצִיא לוֹ שְׁלשֶׁת לֻגִּין שֶׁמֶן לְמֵאָה,
chunks.en: He takes off three lug of oil for each hundred:
chunks.explain: A lug is a small measure.
chunks.st: He deducts three log of oil for one hundred log:

chunks.en: a lug and a half for the dregs at the bottom,
chunks.st: A log and a half for sediment that sinks to the bottom of the cask,

chunks.en: and a lug and a half soaked into the barrel.
chunks.st: and a log and a half for absorption into the cask.

chunks.en: If it was clear, filtered oil,
chunks.st: If it was refined oil,

chunks.en: he does not take off for dregs.
chunks.st: he does not deduct any of the oil for sediment because it was filtered.

chunks.en: If the barrels were old,
chunks.st: If the oil was stored in old casks that are already saturated,

chunks.en: he does not take off for soaking in.
chunks.explain: Old barrels are already full of oil and soak up no more.
chunks.st: he does not deduct any of the oil for absorption.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even someone who sells filtered oil
chunks.st: Even in a case of one who sells refined oil

chunks.en: to his friend all year round,
chunks.st: to another all the days of the year,

chunks.en: the buyer accepts on himself
chunks.st: this buyer accepts upon himself that the seller will deduct

chunks.en: a lug and a half of dregs for each hundred.
chunks.st: a log and a half of sediment for one hundred log, as that is the standard measure of sediment.

mishnayos.summary: A watchman moved a barrel he was watching and it broke. Whether he pays depends on whether he moved it for himself or for the barrel, whether it broke in his hand, and whether the owner gave it a set place.

chunks.en: If someone left a barrel with his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits a barrel with another,

chunks.en: and the owner did not set a place for it,
chunks.st: and the owners did not designate a specific place for the barrel to be stored in the bailee’s house,

chunks.en: and he moved it and it broke:
chunks.st: and the bailee moved it and it broke,

chunks.en: if it broke in his hand,
chunks.st: if it broke while still in his hand,

chunks.en: if he moved it for himself, he must pay;
chunks.st: there is a distinction: If he moved the barrel for his purposes, he is liable to pay for the damage.

chunks.en: if for the barrel's good, he is free.
chunks.st: If he moved the barrel for its own purposes, to prevent it from being damaged, he is exempt.

chunks.en: If it broke after he put it down,
chunks.st: If, after he replaced the barrel it broke,

chunks.en: whether for himself or for the barrel, he is free.
chunks.st: whether he initially moved it for his purposes or whether he moved it for its own purposes, he is exempt.

chunks.en: If the owner set a place for it,
chunks.st: But if the owners designated a specific place for the barrel,

chunks.en: and he moved it and it broke,
chunks.st: and the bailee moved it and it broke,

chunks.en: whether in his hand or after he put it down:
chunks.st: whether it broke while still in his hand or whether it broke after he replaced the barrel,

chunks.en: if for himself, he must pay;
chunks.st: if he moved it for his purposes he is liable to pay,

chunks.en: if for the barrel's good, he is free.
chunks.st: and if he moved it for its own purposes, he is exempt.

mishnayos.summary: A watchman who did not guard coins the way watchmen normally do must pay if they are lost. If he guarded them properly, he does not pay.

chunks.en: If someone left coins with his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposited coins with another,

chunks.en: and he tied them up and hung them behind his back,
chunks.st: and that bailee bound it in a cloth and slung it behind him,

chunks.en: or gave them to his young son or daughter,
chunks.st: or conveyed them to his minor son or daughter for safeguarding,

chunks.en: or locked the door in front of them in a bad way,
chunks.st: or locked the door before them in an inappropriate, i.e., insufficient, manner to secure them,

chunks.en: he must pay, because he did not guard the way watchmen guard.
chunks.st: the bailee is liable to pay for the coins, as he did not safeguard the coins in the manner typical of bailees.

chunks.en: But if he guarded the way watchmen guard, he is free.
chunks.st: But if he safeguarded the money in the manner that bailees safeguard items and it was nevertheless stolen, he is exempt.

mishnayos.summary: If money left with a money changer is tied up, he may not use it; if it is loose, he may, and then he must pay if it is lost. A regular person may never use it; the Tannaim argue about a storekeeper.

chunks.en: If someone leaves coins with a money changer,
chunks.st: In the case of one who deposits money with a money changer,

chunks.en: if they are tied up,
chunks.st: if the money is bound,

chunks.en: he may not use them,
chunks.st: the money changer may not use it.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן,
chunks.en: so if they get lost, he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: Therefore, if it is lost he does not bear responsibility for it.

chunks.en: If they are loose, he may use them,
chunks.explain: The owner knows a money changer uses coins.
chunks.st: If the money was unbound, the money changer may use it.

chunks.en: so if they get lost, he must pay.
chunks.st: Therefore, if it is lost he bears responsibility for it.

chunks.en: If they were left with a regular person,
chunks.st: If he deposited money with a homeowner,

chunks.en: whether tied up or loose,
chunks.st: whether it is bound or whether it is unbound,

chunks.en: he may not use them,
chunks.st: the homeowner may not use it,
chunks.stMore: as it never entered the mind of the depositor that the homeowner might use the money.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ אֵינוֹ חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן.
chunks.en: so if they get lost, he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: Therefore, if the homeowner lost the money, he does not bear responsibility for it.

chunks.en: A storekeeper is like a regular person.
chunks.st: If the bailee is a storekeeper, his status is like that of a homeowner;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: a storekeeper is like a money changer.
chunks.st: If the bailee is a storekeeper, his status is like that of a money changer.

mishnayos.summary: A watchman who used a deposit for himself must pay for it, and the Tannaim argue about which value he pays. Only really using it makes him responsible, and lifting a barrel counts as taking all of it.

chunks.en: If a watchman uses a deposit for himself,
chunks.explain: He takes what he is watching for his own use.
chunks.st: With regard to one who misappropriates a deposit,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he loses out whether its value went down or up.
chunks.explain: He pays whichever value is higher.
chunks.st: He is penalized for its decrease and its increase.
chunks.stMore: If the value of the deposit decreases, the bailee is liable to pay in accordance with its value at the time of the misappropriation. If it increases in value, he is liable to pay in accordance with its value at the time of repayment.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he pays what it was worth when he took it.
chunks.st: He pays in accordance with its value at the time of removal.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: what it was worth when the owner asks for it.
chunks.st: He pays in accordance with its value at the time of the claim.

chunks.en: If someone plans to use a deposit for himself,
chunks.st: With regard to one who intends to misappropriate a deposit and voices that intent in the presence of witnesses,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say he must pay.
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: He is liable to pay for any damage to the deposit from that point forward,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁלַח בּוֹ יָד,
chunks.en: he does not pay until he really uses it,
chunks.st: He is liable to pay only if he actually misappropriates the deposit,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated concerning a bailee:

chunks.he: אִם לֹא שָׁלַח יָדוֹ בִּמְלֶאכֶת רֵעֵהוּ.
chunks.en: "if he did not put his hand on his friend's things."
chunks.st: “Whether he has misappropriated his neighbor’s goods” (Exodus 22:7).

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. הִטָּה אֶת הֶחָבִית וְנָטַל הֵימֶנָּה רְבִיעִית,
chunks.en: How so? If he tipped the barrel and took a revi'is from it,
chunks.explain: A revi'is is a small cup of wine.
chunks.st: If he tilted the deposited barrel and took from it a quarter-log of wine for his own use,

chunks.en: and it broke, he pays only for the revi'is.
chunks.st: and the barrel broke, then he pays only for that quarter-log.

chunks.en: If he lifted it and took a revi'is from it,
chunks.st: If he lifted the barrel and took from it a quarter-log of wine,

chunks.en: and it broke, he pays for all of it.
chunks.explain: Lifting it made it his.
chunks.st: and the barrel broke, since he acquired the barrel by lifting it, he pays the value of the entire barrel.

mishnayos.summary: When people trade coins or things, taking one side finishes the deal. The mishnah teaches which side counts as the "thing" that finishes the deal: gold over silver, copper over silver, worn coins over good ones, blank coins over stamped ones, and goods over coins.

chunks.en: Gold buys silver,
chunks.explain: Taking the gold finishes the deal for the silver.
chunks.st: Therefore, when one party takes possession of the gold coins, the other party acquires the silver coins.

chunks.en: but silver does not buy gold.
chunks.st: But when one party takes possession of the silver coins, the other party does not acquire the gold coins.

chunks.en: Copper buys silver,
chunks.st: In an exchange of silver coins for copper coins, when one party takes possession of the copper coins, the other party acquires the silver coins.

chunks.en: but silver does not buy copper.
chunks.st: But when one party takes possession of the silver coins, the other party does not acquire the copper coins.

chunks.en: Worn-out coins buy good ones,
chunks.st: In an exchange of flawed coins for unflawed coins, when one party takes possession of the flawed coins, the other party acquires the unflawed coins.

chunks.en: but good ones do not buy worn-out ones.
chunks.st: But when one party takes possession of the unflawed coins, the other party does not acquire the flawed coins.

chunks.en: A blank coin buys a stamped coin,
chunks.explain: A blank coin is metal not yet stamped as money.
chunks.st: In an exchange of an unminted coin for a minted coin, when one party takes possession of an unminted coin [asimon], the other party acquires a minted coin.

chunks.en: but a stamped coin does not buy a blank coin.
chunks.st: But when one party takes possession of a minted coin, the other party does not acquire an unminted coin.

chunks.en: Things buy coins,
chunks.st: In an exchange of a coin for movable property, when one party takes possession of the movable property the other party acquires the coin.

chunks.en: but coins do not buy things.
chunks.st: But when one party takes possession of the coin, the other party does not acquire the movable property.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.he: כָּל הַמִּטַּלְטְלִין קוֹנִין זֶה אֶת זֶה:
chunks.en: all things buy each other.
chunks.explain: When two people swap things, taking one finishes the whole swap.
chunks.st: With regard to those who exchange all forms of movable property, each acquires the property of the other,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the moment that one of the parties to the exchange takes possession of the item that he is acquiring, e.g., by means of pulling, the other party acquires the item from the first party.

mishnayos.stIntro: There is a halakhic principle that when one purchases an item, the payment of the money does not effect the transaction. The transaction is effected only by means of the buyer’s physically taking the item into his possession, e.g., by pulling the item. Payment of money by the buyer creates only a moral obligation for the seller to sell him the item. When two types of currency are exchanged for each other, one of the types will have the status of the money being paid, and the other will have the status of the item being purchased. Handing over the former will not effect the transaction, while handing over the latter will. The mishna teaches: When one purchases gold coins, paying with silver coins, the gold coins assume the status of the purchased item and the silver coins assume the status of money.

mishnayos.summary: A buyer who took the fruit cannot back out, but if he only paid, either side can back out. Still, Hashem punishes a person who does not keep his word. Rabbi Shimon says whoever holds the money has the upper hand.

chunks.en: How so?
chunks.st: How so?

chunks.en: If he pulled the fruit from him
chunks.explain: Pulling the thing toward himself is a way of buying it.
chunks.st: If the buyer pulled produce from the seller,

chunks.en: and did not give him money yet,
chunks.st: but the buyer did not yet give the seller their value in money,

chunks.en: he cannot back out.
chunks.st: he cannot renege on the transaction,

chunks.en: If he gave him money
chunks.st: but if the buyer gave the seller money

chunks.en: and did not pull the fruit from him yet,
chunks.st: but did not yet pull produce from him,

chunks.en: he can back out.
chunks.st: he can renege on the transaction, as the transaction is not yet complete.

chunks.en: But the Sages said:
chunks.st: But with regard to the latter case, the Sages said:

chunks.en: The One Who punished the people of the generation of the Flood
chunks.st: He Who exacted payment from the people of the generation of the flood,

chunks.en: and the generation of the Tower of Bavel
chunks.st: and from the generation of the dispersion, i.e., that of the Tower of Babel,

chunks.en: will punish
chunks.st: will in the future exact payment

chunks.en: whoever does not keep his word.
chunks.st: from whoever does not stand by his statement.
chunks.stMore: Just as the people of those generations were not punished by an earthly court but were subjected to divine punishment, so too, although no earthly court can compel the person who reneged to complete the transaction, punishment will be exacted at the hand of Heaven for any damage that he caused.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: whoever has the money in his hand
chunks.st: Anyone who has the money in his possession

chunks.en: has the upper hand.
chunks.explain: The seller may back out, but the buyer who paid may not.
chunks.st: has the advantage.
chunks.stMore: The Sages said it is only with regard to the seller that payment of money does not effect a transaction, so that if the buyer paid for the item and did not yet take possession of the purchase item, the seller can renege on the sale and return the money. By contrast, once the buyer paid for the item he cannot renege on his decision and demand return of his money, even if he did not yet take possession of the purchase item.

mishnayos.summary: Overcharging means a price off by a sixth, and the buyer can return it until he has time to show a merchant or relative. Rabbi Tarfon ruled a third and a whole day, but the merchants of Lod asked to go back to the Sages' rule.

chunks.en: Overcharging is four silver coins
chunks.explain: Overcharging is selling for too much or too little.
chunks.st: The measure of exploitation for which one can claim that he was exploited is four silver ma’a

chunks.en: out of twenty-four silver coins in a sela,
chunks.st: from the twenty-four silver ma’a in a sela,

chunks.en: a sixth of the price.
chunks.st: or one-sixth of the transaction.

chunks.en: Until when may he return it?
chunks.st: Until when is it permitted for the buyer to return the item?

chunks.he: עַד כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לְתַגָּר אוֹ לִקְרוֹבוֹ.
chunks.en: Until he has time to show it to a merchant or to his relative.
chunks.explain: They know the right price.
chunks.st: He may return it only until a period of time has passed that would allow him to show the merchandise to a merchant or to his relative
chunks.stMore: who is more familiar with the market price of merchandise. If more time has elapsed he can no longer return the item, as the assumption is that he waived his right to receive the sum of the disparity. The mishna continues:

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon taught in Lod:
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon ruled in Lod:

chunks.en: overcharging is eight silver coins for a sela,
chunks.st: Exploitation is a measure of eight silver ma’a from the twenty-four silver ma’a of a sela,

chunks.en: a third of the price.
chunks.st: one-third of the transaction.

chunks.en: And the merchants of Lod were happy.
chunks.explain: They could charge more without the sale being undone.
chunks.st: And the merchants of Lod rejoiced,
chunks.stMore: as this ruling allowed them a greater profit margin and rendered the nullification of a transaction less likely.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon said to them:

chunks.en: "One may return it the whole day."
chunks.st: Throughout the entire day it is permitted to renege
chunks.stMore: on the transaction and not merely for the period of time it takes to show the purchase item to a merchant or a relative.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The merchants of Lod said to him:

chunks.en: "Let Rabbi Tarfon leave us the way we were."
chunks.st: Let Rabbi Tarfon leave us as we were, with the previous ruling,

chunks.en: And they went back to the words of the Sages.
chunks.st: and they reverted to following the statement of the Rabbis in the mishna with regard to both rulings.

mishnayos.summary: Both buyers and sellers are protected from overcharging, and Rabbi Yehuda says a merchant is not. The one who was cheated can choose to undo the sale or get back the extra.

chunks.en: Both the buyer and the seller
chunks.st: Both the buyer and the seller are

chunks.en: are protected by the law of overcharging.
chunks.st: subject to the halakhot of exploitation.

chunks.en: Just as overcharging counts for a regular person,
chunks.st: Just as the halakhot of exploitation apply to a layman,

chunks.en: so it counts for a merchant.
chunks.st: so do the halakhot of exploitation apply to a merchant.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: there is no overcharging for a merchant.
chunks.explain: A merchant knows prices well.
chunks.st: There is no exploitation for a merchant, as he is an expert in the market price of merchandise.

chunks.en: The one who was cheated
chunks.st: The one upon whom the exploitation was imposed

chunks.en: has the upper hand.
chunks.st: has the advantage.

chunks.en: If he wants, he says, "Give me my money back,"
chunks.st: If he wishes, he can say to the other: Give me back my money and nullify the transaction,

chunks.en: or, "Give me back the extra you cheated me."
chunks.st: or he can say: Give me back the sum that you gained by exploiting me.

mishnayos.summary: How worn down can a sela coin be before using it at full value counts as overcharging? Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon each give a different amount.

chunks.en: How much can a sela coin be worn down
chunks.st: How much can the sela coin be eroded through usage,

chunks.en: and still not be overcharging?
chunks.st: and its use in a transaction at its original value will still not constitute exploitation?

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: four issars,
chunks.explain: An issar is a small coin.
chunks.st: The accepted depreciation is four issar,

chunks.en: one issar for each dinar.
chunks.st: which is a rate of one issar per dinar, or one twenty-fourth of a dinar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: four pundyons,
chunks.explain: A pundyon is worth two issars.
chunks.st: The accepted depreciation is four pundeyon,

chunks.en: one pundyon for each dinar.
chunks.st: which is a rate of one pundeyon per dinar, or one-twelfth of a dinar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: eight pundyons,
chunks.st: The accepted depreciation is eight pundeyon,

chunks.en: two pundyons for each dinar.
chunks.st: which is a rate of two pundeyon per dinar, or one-sixth of a dinar.

mishnayos.summary: The mishnah teaches how long one may return a worn coin. The one who gave it must take it back if he knows it, and such a coin may be used for ma'aser sheni.

chunks.en: Until when may he return it?
chunks.st: The mishna continues: Until when is it permitted for one to return a worn coin once he realizes that it is defective?

chunks.en: In big cities, until he has time to show it to a money changer.
chunks.st: In the cities [bakerakim], one may return it only until a period of time has passed that would allow him to show it to a money changer, who is an expert in matters of coins.

chunks.en: In villages, until Erev Shabbos.
chunks.explain: That is when people shop and find out.
chunks.st: In the villages, where there is no money changer, one may return it only until Shabbat eves,
chunks.stMore: when people purchase their Shabbat needs. Although these are the limits of how much a coin must be eroded in order for there to be exploitation,

chunks.en: If he recognizes it as his coin,
chunks.st: if the one who gave the coin to the aggrieved party recognized it,

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ מְקַבְּלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ,
chunks.en: he must take it back from him even after twelve months,
chunks.st: he must accept it back from him even after twelve months have passed no matter how little the erosion affected its value.

chunks.en: and he can only complain about him.
chunks.st: And he has only a grievance against him, as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: And he may use it for ma'aser sheni and not worry,
chunks.explain: Ma'aser sheni money is used for food in Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: And one may give the slightly eroded coin for use in the desacralizing of second-tithe produce and he need not be concerned,

chunks.en: since only a stingy person would refuse it.
chunks.st: as one who would refuse to accept a slightly eroded coin is merely a miserly soul, while the coin is in fact valid for any use.

mishnayos.summary: The mishnah lists amounts: overcharging, a claim and admission in beis din, and five laws that use a perutah, the smallest coin.

chunks.en: Overcharging is four silver coins,
chunks.st: The measure of exploitation is four silver ma’a from the twenty-four silver ma’a of a sela.

chunks.en: a claim in beis din is two silver coins,
chunks.explain: That is the smallest claim that leads to an oath.
chunks.st: And the smallest monetary claim in court for which a plaintiff can obligate a respondent to take an oath is two silver ma’a.

chunks.en: and an admission is a perutah's worth.
chunks.explain: A perutah is the smallest coin.
chunks.st: And the smallest monetary admission for which that respondent takes the oath is an admission that one owes at least the value of one peruta.

chunks.en: There are five things with a perutah:
chunks.st: On a related note, the tanna adds that there are five halakhic situations involving perutot:

chunks.en: An admission is a perutah's worth,
chunks.st: The admission to part of a claim must be that one owes at least the value of one peruta,

chunks.en: a woman can become married with a perutah's worth,
chunks.st: and a woman is betrothed with the value of one peruta.

chunks.he: וְהַנֶּהֱנֶה בְשָׁוֶה פְרוּטָה מִן הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ מָעַל,
chunks.en: one who uses a perutah's worth of hekdesh did me'ilah,
chunks.explain: Hekdesh is what belongs to the Beis HaMikdash; me'ilah is misusing it.
chunks.st: And one who derives benefit of the value of one peruta from consecrated property has misused consecrated property and is liable to bring an offering,

chunks.en: one who finds a perutah's worth must announce it,
chunks.st: and one who finds an item that has the value of one peruta is obligated to proclaim that he found it.

chunks.en: and if someone robs a perutah's worth from his friend
chunks.st: And with regard to one who robs from another an item that has the value of one peruta

chunks.en: and swears falsely to him,
chunks.st: and took an oath to him
chunks.stMore: that he robbed nothing, when he repents and seeks to return the stolen item

chunks.en: he must bring it to him, even as far as Madai.
chunks.explain: Madai is a far-away land.
chunks.st: he must take it and follow its owner even to Media.
chunks.stMore: In that case, he may not return the item by means of a messenger; he must give it directly to its owner.

mishnayos.summary: There are five times when someone must add a fifth to what he pays, like when he eats terumah by mistake, redeems his own ma'aser sheni or hekdesh, or robs and swears falsely.

chunks.en: There are five times one adds a fifth:
chunks.st: There are five halakhic situations where one-fifth is added to the value of the principal, and these are they:

chunks.en: One who eats terumah,
chunks.explain: A person who is not a Kohen ate it by mistake.
chunks.st: A non-priest who eats either teruma,

chunks.en: or terumas ma'aser,
chunks.explain: The Levi gives this part of his ma'aser to a Kohen.
chunks.st: or teruma of the tithe, which the Levite separates from the first tithe and gives to a priest,

chunks.en: or terumas ma'aser from demai,
chunks.explain: Demai is food that may not have been tithed.
chunks.st: or teruma of the tithe of demai,

chunks.en: or challah, or bikkurim, adds a fifth.
chunks.st: or ḥalla, or first fruits; in each of these cases, he adds one-fifth when paying restitution to the priest who owned the produce.

chunks.he: וְהַפּוֹדֶה נֶטַע רְבָעִי וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלּוֹ,
chunks.en: And one who redeems his own fourth-year fruit or ma'aser sheni
chunks.explain: To redeem is to move its holiness onto money.
chunks.st: And one who redeems his own fruit of a fourth-year sapling or second-tithe produce

chunks.en: adds a fifth.
chunks.st: adds one-fifth.

chunks.en: One who redeems his own hekdesh
chunks.st: One who redeems his own consecrated property

chunks.en: adds a fifth.
chunks.st: adds one-fifth.

chunks.en: One who uses a perutah's worth of hekdesh
chunks.st: One who derives benefit worth one peruta from consecrated property

chunks.en: adds a fifth.
chunks.st: adds one-fifth.

chunks.en: And one who robs a perutah's worth from his friend
chunks.st: And one who robs the value of one peruta from another

chunks.en: and swears falsely to him
chunks.st: and takes a false oath in response to his claim

chunks.en: adds a fifth.
chunks.st: adds one-fifth when paying restitution.

mishnayos.stIntro: In this mishna, as in the previous one, the tanna enumerates several halakhot that share a common element.

mishnayos.summary: Some things, like servants, documents, land and hekdesh, do not follow the rules of overcharging, double payment, or the watchmen's rules. The Tannaim argue about korbanos, a Sefer Torah, an animal and a pearl.

chunks.en: These are things that have no overcharging:
chunks.st: These are matters that are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation
chunks.stMore: even if the disparity between the value and the payment is one-sixth or greater:

chunks.en: servants, documents,
chunks.st: Slaves, and documents,

chunks.en: land, and hekdesh.
chunks.st: and land, and consecrated property.

chunks.en: They have no double payment,
chunks.st: In addition, if they are stolen, these items are subject neither to payment of double the principal for theft

chunks.en: and no payment of four or five.
chunks.st: nor to payment of four or five
chunks.stMore: times the principal, if the thief slaughtered or sold a stolen sheep or cow, respectively.

chunks.en: A free watchman does not swear for them,
chunks.st: An unpaid bailee does not take an oath

chunks.en: and a paid watchman does not pay.
chunks.st: and a paid bailee does not pay if these items were stolen or lost.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: korbanos that he must replace if lost
chunks.st: With regard to sacrificial animals for which one bears responsibility to replace them,

chunks.en: have overcharging,
chunks.st: they are subject to the halakhot of exploitation, as this responsibility indicates a certain aspect of ownership.

chunks.en: and those he does not have to replace
chunks.st: And those for which one does not bear responsibility to replace them,

chunks.en: have no overcharging.
chunks.st: they are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even one who sells a Sefer Torah,
chunks.st: Even in the case of one who sells a Torah scroll,

chunks.en: an animal, or a pearl,
chunks.st: an animal, or a pearl,

chunks.en: there is no overcharging for them.
chunks.explain: They have no set price.
chunks.st: these items are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation, as they have no fixed price.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: "They said only these."
chunks.st: The early Sages stated that only these items listed above are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation.

mishnayos.summary: Hurting someone with words is like cheating him in a sale. Do not ask a price when you do not want to buy, and do not remind a ba'al teshuvah or a child of geirim of their past.

chunks.en: Just as there is cheating in buying and selling,
chunks.st: Just as there is a prohibition against exploitation [ona’a] in buying and selling,

chunks.en: so there is cheating with words.
chunks.explain: Saying things that hurt someone's feelings.
chunks.st: so is there ona’a in statements,
chunks.stMore: i.e., verbal mistreatment. The mishna proceeds to cite examples of verbal mistreatment.

chunks.he: לֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ בְּכַמָּה חֵפֶץ זֶה,
chunks.en: One should not ask the seller, "How much is this thing?"
chunks.st: One may not say to a seller: For how much are you selling this item,

chunks.en: when he does not want to buy.
chunks.st: if he does not wish to purchase
chunks.stMore: it. He thereby upsets the seller when the deal fails to materialize. The mishna lists other examples:

chunks.en: If someone did teshuvah,
chunks.st: If one is a penitent,

chunks.he: לֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ זְכֹר מַעֲשֶׂיךָ הָרִאשׁוֹנִים.
chunks.en: one should not tell him, "Remember what you used to do."
chunks.st: another may not say to him: Remember your earlier deeds.

chunks.en: If someone's parents were geirim,
chunks.explain: Geirim are people who became Jewish.
chunks.st: If one is the child of converts,

chunks.he: לֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ זְכֹר מַעֲשֵׂה אֲבוֹתֶיךָ,
chunks.en: one should not tell him, "Remember what your fathers did,"
chunks.st: another may not say to him: Remember the deeds of your ancestors,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Do not hurt a ger
chunks.st: “And a convert shall you neither mistreat,

chunks.en: and do not press him."
chunks.st: nor shall you oppress him” (Exodus 22:20).

mishnayos.summary: A seller may not mix fruit from different places to trick buyers, but may mix wines to make them better. Watered wine may be sold only if the buyer is told, and never to a merchant, unless that is the local custom.

chunks.en: One may not mix fruit with fruit,
chunks.st: One may not intermingle produce bought from one supplier with other produce,

chunks.en: even new with new,
chunks.st: even if he intermingles new produce with other new produce and ostensibly the buyer suffers no loss from his doing so.

chunks.en: and of course not new with old.
chunks.st: And needless to say, one may not intermingle new produce with old
chunks.stMore: produce, in the event that the old produce is superior, as with grains, since intermingling lowers its value.

chunks.he: בֶּאֱמֶת, בְּיַיִן הִתִּירוּ לְעָרֵב קָשֶׁה בְרַךְ,
chunks.en: Really, for wine they allowed mixing strong with weak,
chunks.st: Actually, they said: With regard to wine, they permitted one to mix strong wine with weak wine,

chunks.en: because it makes it better.
chunks.st: because one thereby enhances it.

chunks.en: One may not mix wine dregs into wine,
chunks.st: One may not intentionally mix wine sediment with the wine,

chunks.en: but he may give him its own dregs.
chunks.st: but one may give the buyer wine with its sediment; the seller is not required to filter the wine.

chunks.en: If water got mixed into someone's wine,
chunks.st: One who had water mix with his wine

chunks.en: he should not sell it in a store unless
chunks.st: may not sell it in the store,

chunks.en: he tells the buyer.
chunks.st: unless he informs the buyer that it contains water.

chunks.he: וְלֹא לְתַגָּר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוֹדִיעוֹ,
chunks.en: And not to a merchant, even if he tells him,
chunks.st: And he may not sell it to a merchant, even if he informs him of the mixture,

chunks.en: because it will only be used to trick people.
chunks.st: as, although he is aware that there is water mixed with the wine, it will be used for nothing other than deceit
chunks.stMore: because the merchant will likely not inform the buyer that it is diluted.

chunks.he: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לְהַטִּיל מַיִם בַּיַּיִן, יַטִּילוּ:
chunks.en: Where people usually put water in wine, they may put it in.
chunks.st: In a place where they are accustomed to place water into the wine to dilute it and everyone is aware of that fact, one may place water in the wine.

mishnayos.summary: A merchant may store grain or wine from different people together if he does not mean to trick anyone. The Sages discuss giving treats to children, lowering prices, sifting beans, and dressing up things to sell.

chunks.en: A merchant may take from five threshing floors
chunks.st: a merchant may take grain from five threshing floors belonging to different people,

chunks.en: and put it in one storehouse.
chunks.st: and place the produce in one warehouse.

chunks.en: From five winepresses
chunks.st: He may also take wine from five winepresses

chunks.en: into one barrel,
chunks.st: and place the wine in one large cask [pitom],

chunks.en: as long as he does not mean to mix bad with good.
chunks.st: provided that he does not intend to mix low-quality merchandise with high-quality merchandise.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: לֹא יְחַלֵּק הַחֶנְוָנִי קְלָיוֹת וֶאֱגוֹזִין לַתִּינוֹקוֹת,
chunks.en: A storekeeper should not hand out roasted grain and nuts to children,
chunks.st: A storekeeper may not hand out toasted grain and nuts to children who patronize his store,

chunks.en: because he gets them used to coming to him.
chunks.explain: Then they will not go to other stores.
chunks.st: due to the fact that he thereby accustoms them to come to him at the expense of competing storekeepers.

chunks.en: But the Sages allow it.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis permit doing so.

chunks.en: And he should not lower the price.
chunks.st: And one may not reduce the price of sale items below the market rate.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he should be remembered for good.
chunks.explain: Cheaper prices help poor people.
chunks.st: If he wishes to do so, he should be remembered positively.

chunks.en: He should not sift the ground beans;
chunks.explain: Then he might charge more than they are worth.
chunks.st: One may not sift ground beans
chunks.stMore: to remove the waste, lest he charge an inappropriately high price for the sifted meal, beyond its actual value;

chunks.en: these are the words of Abba Shaul.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Abba Shaul.

chunks.en: But the Sages allow it.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis permit doing so.

chunks.he: וּמוֹדִים שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹר מֵעַל פִּי מְגוּרָה,
chunks.en: And they agree he should not sift just the top of the bin,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis concede that one may not sift the meal only from the beans that are close to the opening of the bin
chunks.stMore: to create the impression that the contents of the entire bin were sifted,

chunks.en: because that is just fooling the eye.
chunks.st: as this is nothing other than deception.

chunks.en: We do not dress up a person,
chunks.explain: To make something look better than it is when selling it.
chunks.st: One may neither adorn a person before selling him on the slave market,

chunks.he: וְלֹא אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה וְלֹא אֶת הַכֵּלִים:
chunks.en: or an animal, or vessels.
chunks.st: nor an animal nor vessels
chunks.stMore: that he seeks to sell. Rather, they must be sold unembellished, to avoid deceiving the buyer.

mishnayos.stIntro: The prohibition against mixing different types of produce applies only to an individual selling the produce of his field. By contrast,

mishnayos.summary: The Torah forbids ribbis, getting paid extra for a loan. The mishnah shows two kinds: lending money or wheat to get more back, and a tricky wheat-for-wine deal that brings in extra.

chunks.en: What is neshech and what is tarbis?
chunks.explain: Both are names for ribbis, extra paid for a loan.
chunks.st: Which is neshekh, and which is tarbit?

chunks.en: What is neshech?
chunks.st: Which is the case in which there is neshekh?

chunks.en: One who lends a sela to get back five dinars,
chunks.explain: A sela is worth four dinars.
chunks.st: With regard to one who lends another a sela, worth four dinars, for five dinars to be paid later,

chunks.en: two se'ah of wheat to get back three,
chunks.st: or one who lends another two se’a of wheat for three se’a to be returned later,

chunks.en: this is forbidden, because it is "biting."
chunks.explain: Neshech means a bite.
chunks.st: this is prohibited, as it is taking interest [noshekh].

chunks.en: And what is tarbis?
chunks.st: And which is the case in which there is tarbit?

chunks.en: One who makes more with fruit.
chunks.st: It is the case of one who enters into a transaction that yields an increase in the produce beyond his investment.

chunks.en: How so?
chunks.st: How so?

chunks.he: לָקַח הֵימֶנּוּ חִטִּין בְּדִינַר זָהָב הַכּוֹר,
chunks.en: He bought wheat from him at a gold dinar for a kor,
chunks.st: For example, one acquired wheat from another at the price of one kor of wheat for one gold dinar,
chunks.stMore: worth twenty-five silver dinars, with the wheat to be supplied at a later date,

chunks.en: and that was the price then.
chunks.st: and such was the market price of wheat at the time he acquired it.

chunks.en: Then wheat went up to thirty dinars.
chunks.st: The price of one kor of wheat then increased and stood at thirty dinars.

chunks.en: He said to him, "Give me my wheat,
chunks.st: At that point, the buyer said to the seller: Give me all of my wheat now,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֲנִי רוֹצֶה לְמָכְרָן וְלִקַּח בָּהֶן יָיִן.
chunks.en: because I want to sell it and buy wine with it."
chunks.st: as I wish to sell it and purchase wine with it.

chunks.en: The seller said, "Your wheat
chunks.st: The seller said to him: Since it is ultimately wine that you want, not wheat, each kor of your wheat

chunks.en: counts with me as worth thirty,
chunks.st: is considered by me to be worth thirty dinars,

chunks.en: and you have wine with me for it."
chunks.st: and you have the right to collect its value in wine from me.

chunks.en: But he has no wine.
chunks.explain: If wine goes up, the buyer gets more than he paid.
chunks.st: And in this case, the seller did not have wine
chunks.stMore: in his possession. If wine then appreciates in value, the result will be an interest-bearing transaction, as the buyer collects from the seller wine worth more than the wheat for which he paid.

mishnayos.stIntro: The Torah states the prohibition against taking interest: “And if your brother becomes impoverished, and his hand falters with you, then you shall support him; whether a stranger or a native, he shall live with you. You shall not take from him interest [neshekh] or increase [tarbit]; you shall fear your God and your brother shall live with you. You shall not give him your money with neshekh and with marbit you shall not give him your food” (Leviticus 25:35–37). The mishna asks:

mishnayos.summary: A lender may not get free or cheap rent from the borrower. One may charge more rent for paying later, but may not charge more for a field sold on credit.

chunks.en: One who lends money to his friend
chunks.st: One who lends another money

chunks.en: should not live in his yard for free,
chunks.st: may not reside in the borrower’s courtyard free of charge,

chunks.en: and should not rent from him for less,
chunks.st: nor may he rent living quarters from him at less than the going rate,

chunks.en: because that is ribbis.
chunks.st: because this is interest.
chunks.stMore: The benefit he receives from living on the borrower’s property constitutes the equivalent of an additional payment as interest on the loan.

chunks.en: One may raise the price of rent,
chunks.st: One may increase the price of rent to be received at a later date instead of at an earlier one,

chunks.en: but not the price of a sale.
chunks.st: but one may not similarly increase the price of a sale.

chunks.en: How so? He rented his yard to him,
chunks.st: How so? If a courtyard owner rented his courtyard to a renter,

chunks.en: and said to him,
chunks.st: and the owner said to the renter:

chunks.en: "If you pay me now,
chunks.st: If you give me the payment now,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי הוּא לְךָ בְּעֶשֶׂר סְלָעִים לְשָׁנָה,
chunks.en: it is yours for ten sela'im a year,
chunks.st: the rental is yours for ten sela a year,

chunks.en: but if month by month,
chunks.st: but if you pay on a monthly basis it will cost

chunks.en: a sela each month." This is allowed.
chunks.explain: Rent is paid for each month as it comes.
chunks.st: a sela for each month, equaling twelve sela a year. Such a practice is permitted, despite the fact that he charges more for a monthly payment.

chunks.en: He sold him his field
chunks.st: If a field owner sold his field to a buyer

chunks.en: and said to him,
chunks.st: and said to him:

chunks.en: "If you pay me now,
chunks.st: If you give me the payment now,

chunks.en: it is yours for 1,000 zuz;
chunks.st: it is yours for one thousand dinars, but

chunks.en: if at harvest time,
chunks.st: if you wait and pay me at the time of the harvest,

chunks.en: for 1,200." This is forbidden.
chunks.explain: The extra money is paid for waiting, so it is ribbis.
chunks.st: it is yours for twelve hundred dinars, this transaction is prohibited as interest.

mishnayos.summary: A seller may not let a buyer keep using a field while also letting him take it back whenever he pays. A loan with a field promised after three years is allowed, and Baisos ben Zonin did this.

chunks.en: He sold him the field,
chunks.st: If one sold another a field

chunks.en: and the buyer gave him some of the money,
chunks.st: and the buyer gave him some of the money,

chunks.en: and the seller said to him, "Whenever you want,
chunks.st: and the seller said to him: Whenever you wish,

chunks.he: הָבֵא מָעוֹת וְטֹל אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ, אָסוּר.
chunks.en: bring the money and take what is yours." This is forbidden.
chunks.explain: The buyer eats the fruit while the seller holds his money, like ribbis.
chunks.st: bring the outstanding money and take your field at that point, this is prohibited.

chunks.en: He lent him money with his field as a promise,
chunks.st: If one lent money to another on the basis of the borrower’s field serving as a guarantee,

chunks.en: and said to him,
chunks.st: and said to him:

chunks.en: "If you do not pay me
chunks.st: If you do not give me the money now and instead delay your payment

chunks.en: from now until three years,
chunks.st: from now until three years have passed,

chunks.en: it is mine."
chunks.st: the field is mine,

chunks.en: Then it is his.
chunks.st: then after three years, the field is his.
chunks.stMore: This is permitted even if the field is worth more than the amount of the loan.

chunks.en: And this is what Baisos ben Zonin used to do
chunks.st: And this is what Baitos ben Zunin would do,

chunks.en: with the Sages' approval.
chunks.st: with the consent of the Sages, when he lent money.

mishnayos.summary: One may not give goods or animals to someone to sell or raise for half the profit, unless he also pays him for his work and food. One may share calves and foals until they are partly grown.

chunks.en: We may not set up a storekeeper for half the profit,
chunks.explain: The owner gives him goods to sell and they share the profit.
chunks.st: One may not establish a deal with a storekeeper for half the profits.
chunks.stMore: It is prohibited for one to provide a storekeeper with produce for him to sell in his store, with half the profits going to the lender. In such an arrangement, the storekeeper himself is responsible for half of any loss from the venture, effectively rendering half of the produce as a loan to the storekeeper. The lender remains responsible for the other half of any loss, and the storekeeper provides a service by selling his produce for him. This service, if provided free of charge, is viewed as interest paid for the loan, and is prohibited.

chunks.en: and he should not give money
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not give a storekeeper money

chunks.en: to buy fruit with it for half the profit,
chunks.st: with which to acquire produce for the storekeeper to sell for half the profits.

chunks.en: unless he gives
chunks.st: These activities are both prohibited unless the owner gives

chunks.en: him his pay like a worker.
chunks.explain: Otherwise his free work is like ribbis.
chunks.st: the storekeeper his wages as a salaried laborer
chunks.stMore: hired to sell the produce, after which they can divide the remaining profits.

chunks.en: We may not give chickens to sit on eggs for half,
chunks.st: One may not give eggs to another to place chickens on them in exchange for half the profits,

chunks.en: and we may not price calves and foals for half,
chunks.st: and one may not appraise calves or foals for another to raise them for half the profits.

chunks.en: unless he gives
chunks.st: These activities are both prohibited unless the owner gives

chunks.en: him pay for his work and his food.
chunks.st: the other wages for his toil and the cost of the food
chunks.stMore: he gives to the animals in his temporary care. All this applies when the lender establishes a fixed minimum profit he insists on receiving regardless of what happens to the animals.

chunks.en: But one may take calves and foals for half,
chunks.st: But one may accept calves or foals to raise as a joint venture for half
chunks.stMore: of the earnings, with one side providing the animals and taking full responsibility for losses, and the other providing the work and the sustenance,

chunks.en: and raise them until they are a third grown.
chunks.st: and the one raising them may raise them until they reach one-third
chunks.stMore: of their maturation, at which point they are sold and the profits shared.

chunks.en: And a donkey, until it can carry a load.
chunks.st: And with regard to a donkey, it can be raised in this manner until it is large enough to bear a load.

mishnayos.summary: One may share an animal that works and eats for half the profit, and follow the local custom about the babies. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel allows a calf with its mother, and one may raise the rent on a field.

chunks.en: We may price a cow, a donkey,
chunks.st: One may appraise a cow or a donkey

chunks.he: וְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה וְאוֹכֵל לְמֶחֱצָה.
chunks.en: or any animal that works and eats, for half.
chunks.explain: Its work pays for its food.
