chunks.st: or any item that generates revenue while it eats and give it to another to feed it and take care of it in exchange for one-half
chunks.stMore: the profits, with the one who cares for the animal benefiting from the profits it generates during the period in which he raises it. Afterward, they divide the profit that accrues due to appreciation in the value of the animal and due to the offspring it produces.

chunks.he: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַחֲלֹק אֶת הַוְּלָדוֹת מִיָּד, חוֹלְקִין,
chunks.en: Where people usually split the babies right away, they split them;
chunks.st: In a place where it is customary to divide the offspring immediately upon their birth, they divide them,

chunks.en: where they usually raise them, they raise them.
chunks.st: and in a place where it is customary for the one who cared for the mother to raise the offspring for an additional period of time before dividing them, he shall raise them.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: we may price a calf with its mother
chunks.st: One may appraise a calf together with its mother

chunks.en: and a foal with its mother.
chunks.st: or a foal with its mother
chunks.stMore: even though these young animals do not generate revenue while they eat. The costs of raising the young animal need not be considered.

chunks.en: And one may raise the rent on his field
chunks.explain: When the owner gives money to improve it.
chunks.st: And one may inflate [umafriz] the rental fee paid for his field,

chunks.en: and not worry about ribbis.
chunks.st: and he need not be concerned with regard to the prohibition of interest, as the Gemara will explain.

mishnayos.summary: A "tzon barzel" deal, where the owner never loses, is ribbis with a Jew but allowed with a non-Jew. The mishnah also teaches when a Jew may lend a non-Jew's money.

chunks.en: We may not take "iron sheep" from a Jew,
chunks.explain: The one raising them always pays their full value back, but shares the profit.
chunks.st: One may not accept from a Jew sheep to raise or other items to care for as a guaranteed investment,
chunks.stMore: in which the terms of the transaction dictate that the one accepting the item takes upon himself complete responsibility to repay its value in the event of depreciation or loss, but receives only part of the profit.

chunks.en: because that is ribbis.
chunks.st: This is because it is a loan, as the principal is fixed and always returned to the owner, and any additional sum the owner receives is interest.

chunks.he: אֲבָל מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַנָּכְרִים,
chunks.en: But we may take "iron sheep" from non-Jews,
chunks.st: But one may accept a guaranteed investment from gentiles, as there is no prohibition of interest in transactions with them.

chunks.en: and borrow from them and lend to them with ribbis,
chunks.st: And one may borrow money from them and one may lend money to them with interest.

chunks.en: and the same with a ger toshav.
chunks.explain: A non-Jew who keeps the seven mitzvos of Bnei Noach.
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to a gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav],
chunks.stMore: one may borrow money from him with interest and lend money to him with interest, since he is not a Jew.

chunks.en: A Jew may lend a non-Jew's money
chunks.st: Also, a Jew may serve as a middleman and lend a gentile’s money to another Jew

chunks.en: if the non-Jew knows,
chunks.st: with the knowledge of the gentile,

chunks.en: but not if it is the Jew's own plan.
chunks.st: but not with the knowledge of a Jew, i.e., the middleman himself, as the Gemara will explain.

mishnayos.summary: One may not agree on a price for future fruit until the market price is known, except for things already almost ready. The Tannaim argue about manure and about getting the lowest price of the year.

chunks.en: We may not set a price for fruit
chunks.st: One may not set a price with a buyer for the future delivery of produce

chunks.en: until the market price comes out.
chunks.explain: Paying early for a low price would be like ribbis.
chunks.st: until the market rate is publicized,
chunks.stMore: as, if he is paid for supplying produce at a later date in advance of the publication of the market rate for that type of produce, he may set a price that is too low. The money paid in advance is deemed a loan, and if the initial payment was lower than the later market value, delivery of the produce will constitute interest on the loan.

chunks.en: Once the price came out, we may set a price,
chunks.st: Once the market rate is publicized, the seller may set a price, even if the produce is not yet in his possession.

chunks.en: because even if this one does not have it,
chunks.st: The reason for this is that even though this one, i.e., the seller, does not have any of the produce, that one, someone else,

chunks.en: that one does have it.
chunks.st: has
chunks.stMore: it, and the seller could theoretically acquire the produce now at the price he set.

chunks.en: If he was the first of the harvesters,
chunks.st: If the seller was first among the reapers, having harvested his crop before the market rate was set,

chunks.en: he may set a price with him for a stack of grain,
chunks.st: he may set a price with a buyer as he wishes for a stack of grain that is already in his possession,

chunks.en: for a basket of grapes,
chunks.st: or for a large basket of grapes prepared for pressing into wine,

chunks.en: for a vat of olives,
chunks.st: or for a vat [hama’atan] of olives prepared for pressing into oil,

chunks.en: for a potter's clay balls,
chunks.st: or for the clumps [habeitzim] of clay prepared for use by a potter,

chunks.en: and for lime after it was put in the oven.
chunks.explain: These are almost ready.
chunks.st: or for plaster nearing the end of the manufacturing process at the point after he has sunk it, i.e., baked it, in the kiln.
chunks.stMore: Although the market rate has yet to be set, the seller may nevertheless set a price now for their eventual delivery. The mishna continues:

chunks.en: And he may set a price for manure
chunks.st: And he may set a price with a buyer for manure on

chunks.en: all year round.
chunks.explain: There is always manure around.
chunks.st: any of the days of the year,
chunks.stMore: as the manure will certainly be available and it is therefore viewed as if it is ready.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: we may not set a price for manure
chunks.st: One may set the price of manure

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיְתָה לּוֹ זֶבֶל בָּאַשְׁפָּה.
chunks.en: unless he has manure in his pile.
chunks.st: only if he already had a pile of manure in his dunghill to which the sale can immediately be applied,

chunks.en: But the Sages allow it.
chunks.st: but the Rabbis permit it in all cases.

chunks.en: And he may set a price with him at the best price.
chunks.explain: He gets the cheapest price of the whole year.
chunks.st: And one may also set a price with a buyer at the highest rate,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a large amount of produce sold for the lowest price, stipulating with the seller that the sale price match the lowest market rate for this product during the course of the year.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even if he did not set a price
chunks.st: Even if he did not set a price

chunks.en: with him at the best price,
chunks.st: with him beforehand at the highest rate,

chunks.en: he can say, "Give me at this price,
chunks.st: the buyer may say to the seller: Give me the produce at this rate

chunks.en: or give me back my money."
chunks.st: or give me back my money.
chunks.stMore: Since he did not formally acquire the produce, if the price changed he may withdraw from the transaction.

mishnayos.summary: A landowner may lend wheat to his sharecroppers for planting, to be paid back in wheat, but not for eating. Rabban Gamliel was extra careful and took it back at the lower price.

chunks.en: A person may lend his sharecroppers
chunks.explain: Workers who farm his field for a share of the crop.
chunks.st: A person may lend wheat to his sharecroppers

chunks.en: wheat for wheat, for planting,
chunks.st: in exchange for wheat, for the purpose of seeding,
chunks.stMore: meaning that he may lend them a quantity of wheat with which to seed the field, and at harvest time the sharecropper will add the amount of grain that he borrowed to the landowner’s portion of the yield.

chunks.en: but not for eating.
chunks.st: But he may not lend wheat for the sharecroppers to eat
chunks.stMore: and be paid back with an equivalent quantity because this creates a concern about interest, as the price of wheat may rise.

chunks.he: שֶׁהָיָה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַלְוֶה אֶת אֲרִיסָיו
chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel used to lend his sharecroppers
chunks.st: As Rabban Gamliel would lend wheat to his sharecroppers

chunks.en: wheat for wheat, for planting.
chunks.st: in exchange for wheat, for purposes of seeding,

chunks.en: If he lent when it was expensive and it got cheaper,
chunks.st: and if he lent it at a high price and the price then fell,

chunks.en: or when cheap and it got more expensive,
chunks.st: or if he lent it at an inexpensive price and the price subsequently rose,

chunks.en: he took it back from them at the cheap price.
chunks.st: in all cases he would take it back from them at the inexpensive price.

chunks.en: Not because that is the halachah,
chunks.st: But this was not because this is the halakha;

chunks.en: but because he wanted to be strict with himself.
chunks.st: rather, he wanted to be stringent with himself.

mishnayos.summary: One may not borrow wheat to pay back at harvest time, since the price may rise. A short loan is allowed, but Hillel forbids even that, and even a loaf of bread between neighbors.

chunks.en: A person should not say to his friend,
chunks.st: A person may not say to another:

chunks.en: "Lend me a kor of wheat,
chunks.st: Lend me a kor of wheat

chunks.en: and I will give it back to you at harvest time."
chunks.explain: Wheat might cost more then.
chunks.st: and I will give it back to you at the time the wheat is brought to the granary,
chunks.stMore: as the wheat may increase in value, which would mean that when he gives him back a kor of wheat at the time the wheat is brought to the granary it is worth more than the value of the loan, and he therefore will have paid interest.

chunks.en: But he may say to him,
chunks.st: But he may say to him:

chunks.en: "Lend me until my son comes,
chunks.st: Lend me a kor of wheat for a short period of time, e.g., until my son comes

chunks.en: or until I find the key."
chunks.st: or until I find the key,
chunks.stMore: as there is no concern about a change in price during such a short interval of time.

chunks.en: But Hillel forbids it.
chunks.st: And Hillel prohibits the practice even in this case.

chunks.en: And so Hillel used to say,
chunks.st: And Hillel would similarly say:

chunks.en: "A woman should not lend a loaf to her friend
chunks.st: A woman may not lend a loaf of bread to another

chunks.en: unless she sets its price in money,
chunks.st: unless she establishes its monetary value,

chunks.en: in case wheat goes up in price,
chunks.st: lest the wheat appreciate in value before she returns it,

chunks.en: and they will end up with ribbis."
chunks.st: and they will therefore have come to transgress the prohibition of interest.

mishnayos.summary: Neighbors may trade help with the same kind of work, but not different kinds that may be harder. Rabban Gamliel warns about gifts before or after a loan, and Rabbi Shimon about helpful words.

chunks.en: A person may say to his friend,
chunks.st: A person may say to another:

chunks.en: "Weed with me and I will weed with you,"
chunks.st: Weed the wild growths from my field with me now, and I will weed your field with you at a later stage,

chunks.en: "Hoe with me and I will hoe with you."
chunks.st: or: Till my field with me today and I will till with you on a different day.

chunks.en: But he should not say to him,
chunks.st: But he may not say to him:

chunks.en: "Weed with me and I will hoe with you,"
chunks.st: Weed with me today and I will till with you a different day,

chunks.en: "Hoe with me and I will weed with you."
chunks.explain: One job may be harder, and the extra is like ribbis.
chunks.st: or: Till with me today and I will weed with you,
chunks.stMore: as due to the different nature of the tasks it is possible that one of them will have to work harder than the other did, which is a type of interest, since he repaid him with additional labor.

chunks.en: All the dry days count as one.
chunks.st: All the dry days during the summer, when it does not rain, are viewed as one
chunks.stMore: period, meaning that if they each agreed to work one day, the dry days are viewed as though they were all exactly equal in length, despite the slight differences between them.

chunks.en: All the rainy days count as one.
chunks.st: Similarly, all the rainy days are treated as one period.

chunks.he: לֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ חֲרשׁ עִמִּי בַּגָּרִיד
chunks.en: He should not say to him, "Plow with me in the dry season
chunks.st: But he may not say to him: Plow with me in the dry season

chunks.en: and I will plow with you in the rainy season."
chunks.st: and I will plow with you in the rainy season.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

chunks.he: יֵשׁ רִבִּית מֻקְדֶּמֶת וְיֵשׁ רִבִּית מְאֻחֶרֶת.
chunks.en: there is early ribbis and there is late ribbis.
chunks.st: There is a case of pre-paid interest, and there is also a case of interest paid later, both of which are prohibited.

chunks.en: How so? He hoped to borrow from him,
chunks.st: How so? If he had hopes of borrowing money from him in the future,

chunks.he: וְהָיָה מְשַׁלֵּחַ לוֹ וְאוֹמֵר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתַּלְוֵנִי,
chunks.en: and he sent him a gift and said, "This is so that you will lend to me."
chunks.st: and he sends him money or a gift and says: I am sending you this gift in order that you will lend to me,

chunks.en: That is early ribbis.
chunks.st: this is pre-paid interest.

chunks.he: לָוָה הֵימֶנּוּ וְהֶחֱזִיר לוֹ אֶת מְעוֹתָיו,
chunks.en: He borrowed from him and paid him back,
chunks.st: Similarly, if he borrowed money from him and subsequently returned his money,

chunks.en: and then he sent him a gift and said,
chunks.st: and he later sends a gift to him and says:

chunks.en: "This is for your money that sat with me doing nothing."
chunks.st: I am sending you this gift in order to repay you for your money, which was idle with me, preventing you from earning a profit from it,

chunks.en: That is late ribbis.
chunks.st: this is interest paid later.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: there is ribbis of words.
chunks.st: Not only is there interest consisting of payment of money or items, but there is also verbal interest.

chunks.en: The borrower should not tell the lender,
chunks.st: For example, the borrower may not say to the lender:

chunks.en: "Know that a certain man has come
chunks.explain: News that the lender wants to hear.
chunks.st: You should know that so-and-so has come

chunks.en: from a certain place."
chunks.st: from such and such a place,
chunks.stMore: when he is aware that this information is of significance to his creditor. Since his intention is to provide a benefit to the lender, he has effectively paid him an extra sum for the money he lent him, which constitutes interest.

mishnayos.summary: Everyone who takes part in a loan with ribbis does an aveirah: the lender, the borrower, the guarantor, the witnesses, and the writer too. The mishnah lists the pesukim they break.

chunks.en: And these people break a mitzvah:
chunks.st: And these people violate a prohibition of interest:

chunks.en: the lender, and the borrower,
chunks.st: The lender, and the borrower,

chunks.en: and the guarantor, and the witnesses.
chunks.explain: A guarantor promises to pay if the borrower does not.
chunks.st: and the guarantor, and the witnesses.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: also the writer.
chunks.st: Also the scribe who writes the promissory note violates this prohibition.

chunks.en: They break "Do not give,"
chunks.st: These parties to the transaction violate different prohibtions. Some are in violation of: “You shall not give him your money with interest” (Leviticus 25:37),

chunks.en: and "Do not take from him,"
chunks.st: and of: “Do not take from him interest or increase” (Leviticus 25:36),

chunks.he: וּמִשּׁוּם לֹא תִהְיֶה לוֹ כְּנשֶׁה (שמות כב),
chunks.en: and "Do not be to him like a lender who pushes,"
chunks.st: and of: “Do not be to him as a creditor” (Exodus 22:24),

chunks.en: and "Do not put ribbis on him,"
chunks.st: and of “Do not place interest upon him” (Exodus 22:24),

chunks.he: וּמִשּׁוּם וְלִפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל
chunks.en: and "Do not put a stumbling block before the blind,
chunks.explain: Do not help someone else do an aveirah.
chunks.st: and of: “And you shall not place a stumbling block before the blind,

chunks.en: and fear your God; I am Hashem."
chunks.st: and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord” (Leviticus 19:14).

mishnayos.summary: If workers and an employer fool each other, they can only complain. But if workers back out of a job that cannot wait and no one else can do it, the employer may hire others at their cost or trick them back to work.

chunks.en: If someone hires workers,
chunks.st: With regard to one who hires artisans or laborers,

chunks.en: and they fooled each other,
chunks.st: and they deceived one another,

chunks.he: אֵין לָהֶם זֶה עַל זֶה אֶלָּא תַרְעֹמֶת.
chunks.en: they can only complain about each other.
chunks.explain: Nobody has to pay anything.
chunks.st: they have nothing but a grievance against one another, and they have no financial claim against the deceptive party.

chunks.en: If he hired a donkey driver and a potter
chunks.st: If one hired a donkey driver or a potter

chunks.en: to bring wedding poles and flutes
chunks.st: to bring posts [piryafarin] for a canopy or flutes

chunks.en: for a bride or for a funeral,
chunks.st: to play in honor of a bride or the dead,

chunks.en: or workers to take his flax out of the soaking pool,
chunks.explain: If it stays in the water too long, it spoils.
chunks.st: or if he hired laborers to bring up his flax from the retting tub,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the container of water in which flax is placed in the first stage of the manufacture of linen,

chunks.en: or anything that will be lost if not done in time,
chunks.st: and likewise any matter that involves financial loss if not performed on time

chunks.en: and they backed out,
chunks.st: and the laborers reneged,

chunks.en: in a place where there is no one else,
chunks.st: if this occurred in a place where there is no other person to perform the task,

chunks.en: he may hire others at their cost, or trick them.
chunks.explain: He may promise more pay, but give only what was agreed.
chunks.st: he may hire replacements for a large fee at the expense of the first workers, or deceive them to get them to return to work.

mishnayos.summary: Whoever backs out of a work deal, the workers or the employer, loses out. Whoever changes the deal or backs out is at a disadvantage.

chunks.en: If someone hires workers and they back out,
chunks.st: With regard to one who hires artisans or laborers to perform work and they reneged on the agreement midway through the work,

chunks.en: they have the lower hand.
chunks.explain: They lose out.
chunks.st: they are at a disadvantage. They must ensure that the employer does not suffer a loss.

chunks.en: If the employer backs out,
chunks.st: Conversely, if the employer reneges,

chunks.en: he has the lower hand.
chunks.st: he is at a disadvantage.

chunks.en: Whoever changes the deal
chunks.st: These two rulings are in accordance with the principle that whoever changes the terms accepted by both parties

chunks.en: has the lower hand,
chunks.st: is at a disadvantage,

chunks.en: and whoever backs out
chunks.st: and whoever reneges on an agreement

chunks.en: has the lower hand.
chunks.st: is at a disadvantage.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna states a related halakha:

mishnayos.summary: Someone who rents a donkey must use it the way he agreed. If he took it on a different road and it died, slipped or got too hot, whether he pays depends on whether the change caused it.

chunks.en: If someone rents a donkey to take it
chunks.st: With regard to one who rents a donkey to lead it

chunks.en: on the mountain, and took it in the valley,
chunks.st: on a mountain but he led it in a valley,

chunks.en: or in the valley, and took it on the mountain,
chunks.st: or one who rents a donkey to lead it in a valley but he led it on a mountain,

chunks.en: even if this road is ten mil
chunks.explain: A mil is a measure of distance.
chunks.st: even if this path is ten mil

chunks.en: and that one is ten mil,
chunks.st: and that one is also ten mil,

chunks.en: and it died, he must pay.
chunks.explain: He changed the deal.
chunks.st: and the animal dies, he is liable.

chunks.en: If someone rents a donkey and it got sick,
chunks.st: With regard to one who rents a donkey and it became ill

chunks.en: or it was taken for the king's work,
chunks.st: or was seized for public service [angarya],

chunks.en: the owner says to him, "Here is yours in front of you."
chunks.explain: He does not have to give another donkey.
chunks.st: the owner can say to the renter: That which is yours is before you,
chunks.stMore: and he is not required to reimburse the renter or to supply him with another donkey.

chunks.en: If it died or broke a leg,
chunks.st: If the animal died or its leg broke,

chunks.en: he must give him another donkey.
chunks.st: the owner is obligated to provide the renter with another donkey.

chunks.en: If someone rents a donkey to take it
chunks.st: With regard to one who rents a donkey to lead it

chunks.en: on the mountain, and took it in the valley,
chunks.st: on a mountain but he led it in a valley,

chunks.en: if it slipped, he does not pay;
chunks.explain: The mountain is more slippery anyway.
chunks.st: if it slipped and injured itself he is exempt,

chunks.en: but if it got too hot, he must pay.
chunks.explain: The valley is hotter.
chunks.st: but if it died of heatstroke he is liable, as it was the walk in the hotter valley that caused its death.

chunks.en: If he rented it for the valley and took it on the mountain,
chunks.st: With regard to one who rents a donkey to lead it in a valley but he led it on a mountain,

chunks.en: if it slipped, he must pay;
chunks.st: if it slipped he is liable, because this was caused by the mountainous terrain,

chunks.en: but if it got too hot, he does not pay.
chunks.st: but if it died of heatstroke he is exempt.

chunks.en: If the heat came from the climb, he must pay.
chunks.st: If it suffered from heatstroke due to the ascent, he is liable.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who rents a cow for plowing or threshing and uses it for a different job pays only if the new job was harder on it.

chunks.en: If someone rents a cow to plow
chunks.st: With regard to one who rents a cow and a plow in order

chunks.en: on the mountain, and plowed in the valley,
chunks.st: to plow on the mountain but he plowed in the valley,

chunks.en: if the plow blade broke, he does not pay.
chunks.explain: It would break even more easily on the mountain.
chunks.st: if the plowshare, the cutting tool on the bottom part of the plow, breaks, he is exempt, as it was even more likely to break on mountainous terrain.

chunks.en: If for the valley and he plowed on the mountain,
chunks.st: In a case where he rents the cow and a plow to plow in the valley but he plowed on the mountain,

chunks.en: if the plow blade broke, he must pay.
chunks.st: if the plowshare breaks he is liable.

chunks.en: If to thresh beans and it threshed grain, he does not pay.
chunks.st: If he hired the cow to thresh legumes but it threshed grain, and the cow slipped and broke its leg, he is exempt.

chunks.en: If to thresh grain and it threshed beans, he must pay,
chunks.st: If he hired it to thresh grain but it threshed legumes he is liable,

chunks.en: because beans are slippery.
chunks.st: because legumes are slippery.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who rents a donkey to carry wheat must not load something bulkier or heavier. If he adds more than a small amount to its load, he must pay if it gets hurt.

chunks.he: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר לְהָבִיא עָלֶיהָ חִטִּים
chunks.en: If someone rents a donkey to carry wheat on it
chunks.st: With regard to one who rents a donkey in order to bring wheat on it, to transport it on its back,

chunks.en: and he carried barley on it, he must pay.
chunks.explain: The same weight of barley is much bigger.
chunks.st: and he brought upon it an identical weight of barley, which is lighter than wheat, and the donkey was injured, he is liable.

chunks.en: If grain, and he carried straw on it, he must pay,
chunks.st: Similarly, if he hired it for transporting grain, and he brought straw of the same weight upon it, he is liable,

chunks.en: because the bigger size is as hard as the weight.
chunks.st: because the extra volume is as difficult for the animal as the load itself.

chunks.en: If to carry a lesech of wheat,
chunks.explain: A lesech is an amount, like a big basket.
chunks.st: If he rented a donkey in order to bring on it a letekh, i.e., a measurement of volume, of wheat,

chunks.en: and he carried a lesech of barley, he does not pay.
chunks.explain: That is lighter.
chunks.st: but he brought a letekh of barley, he is exempt, as he brought the same volume of a lighter substance.

chunks.en: And if he added to its load, he must pay.
chunks.st: And one who adds to a load a greater volume than he stipulated is liable.

chunks.he: וְכַמָּה יוֹסִיף עַל מַשָּׂאוֹ וִיהֵא חַיָּב.
chunks.en: And how much must he add to have to pay?
chunks.st: And how much must he add to the load for him to be liable?

chunks.en: Sumchos says in the name of Rabbi Meir,
chunks.st: Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:

chunks.en: a se'ah for a camel,
chunks.st: A se’a on a camel and

chunks.en: three kav for a donkey.
chunks.st: three kav on a donkey.

mishnayos.summary: Workers who take things home to fix are paid watchmen. Once they say "take it and pay me," they are free watchmen. People who watch for each other are paid watchmen.

chunks.en: All workers
chunks.st: All artisans and laborers who take raw materials to their homes

chunks.en: are paid watchmen.
chunks.explain: A paid watchman must take more care.
chunks.st: are considered paid bailees for those items until they return them to the owner.

chunks.en: And any of them who said,
chunks.st: And with regard to all those who said to the owner:

chunks.en: "Take what is yours and bring money,"
chunks.st: I finished the work, and therefore take what is yours, i.e., this item, and bring money in its stead,

chunks.en: is a free watchman.
chunks.st: from that point on each of them is considered an unpaid bailee.

chunks.en: "Watch for me and I will watch for you"
chunks.st: If one person says to another: Safeguard my property for me and I will safeguard your property for you,

chunks.en: is a paid watchman.
chunks.explain: Each one's watching pays the other.
chunks.st: each of them is a paid bailee,
chunks.stMore: as each receives the services of the other as payment for his safeguarding.

chunks.en: "Watch for me,"
chunks.st: If one says: Safeguard for me,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "Put it in front of me,"
chunks.st: and the other says to him: Place it before me,

chunks.en: is a free watchman.
chunks.st: the second individual is an unpaid bailee.

mishnayos.summary: A lender holding a security for a loan is a paid watchman for it; Rabbi Yehuda splits money loans and fruit loans. Abba Shaul lets a lender rent out a poor man's security to pay off his loan.

chunks.en: If he lent him money with a security,
chunks.explain: Something the borrower gives to keep until he pays.
chunks.st: One who lent to another based on collateral

chunks.en: he is a paid watchman for it.
chunks.st: is a paid bailee for the collateral.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If he lent him money,
chunks.st: One who lent another money

chunks.en: he is a free watchman.
chunks.st: is an unpaid bailee for the collateral,

chunks.en: If he lent him fruit,
chunks.st: whereas one who lent another produce

chunks.en: he is a paid watchman.
chunks.st: is a paid bailee.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says,
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:

chunks.he: מֻתָּר אָדָם לְהַשְׂכִּיר מַשְׁכּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עָנִי
chunks.en: a person may rent out a poor man's security,
chunks.st: It is permitted for a person to rent out a poor person’s collateral that was given to him for a loan,

chunks.en: setting a price for it and taking it off the loan,
chunks.st: so that by setting a rental price for it he will thereby progressively
chunks.stMore: reduce the debt, i.e., the lender will subtract the rental money he receives from the amount owed by the borrower,

chunks.en: because it is like returning a lost thing.
chunks.explain: The poor man's loan gets smaller.
chunks.st: because this is considered like returning a lost item.
chunks.stMore: The borrower profits from this arrangement, whereas if the lender does not use the collateral in this manner it provides benefit to no one.

mishnayos.summary: Someone moving a barrel he was watching broke it. The Tanna Kamma says any watchman can swear he was not careless; Rabbi Eliezer was surprised by this ruling.

chunks.en: If someone was moving a barrel from place to place and broke it,
chunks.st: With regard to one who was transporting a barrel from one place to another and he broke it,

chunks.he: בֵּין שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם בֵּין שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר, יִשָּׁבַע.
chunks.en: whether a free watchman or a paid watchman, he swears.
chunks.explain: He swears he was not careless, and does not pay.
chunks.st: whether he was an unpaid bailee or a paid bailee, if he takes an oath that he was not negligent he is exempt from payment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: "Both of them swear,
chunks.st: Both this one, an unpaid bailee, and that one, a paid bailee, must take an oath to exempt themselves from payment,

chunks.en: but I wonder if
chunks.st: but I wonder whether both

chunks.en: both of them can swear."
chunks.explain: This is what he learned from his rebbeim, but he did not understand it.
chunks.st: this one and that one can take an oath.
chunks.stMore: In other words, this is the halakha that I heard from my teachers, but I do not understand their ruling.

mishnayos.summary: An employer must follow the local custom about work hours and food for workers. Rabbi Yochanan ben Masya taught his son that workers, as children of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, deserve the best unless agreed otherwise.

chunks.en: If someone hires workers and tells them
chunks.st: With regard to one who hires laborers and tells

chunks.en: to start very early and stay very late,
chunks.st: them to rise exceptionally early and to continue working until exceptionally late,

chunks.he: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַשְׁכִּים וְשֶׁלֹּא לְהַעֲרִיב,
chunks.en: where people are not used to starting early or staying late,
chunks.st: if this is in a locale where laborers are not accustomed to rising so early or to continuing to work until so late,

chunks.en: he may not force them.
chunks.st: the employer is not permitted to compel them to do so.

chunks.en: Where people usually feed workers, he must feed them.
chunks.st: In a locale where employers are accustomed to feeding their laborers, the employer must feed them.

chunks.en: To give sweets, he must give.
chunks.st: If they are in a locale where an employer is accustomed to providing their laborers with sweet foods, he must provide such food.

chunks.en: Everything follows the custom of the place.
chunks.st: Everything is in accordance with the regional custom in these matters.

chunks.en: There was a story with Rabbi Yochanan ben Masya
chunks.st: There was an incident involving Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Matya,

chunks.en: who said to his son,
chunks.st: who said to his son:

chunks.en: "Go out and hire workers for us."
chunks.st: Go out and hire laborers for us.

chunks.en: He went and promised them food.
chunks.st: His son went, hired them, and pledged to provide sustenance for them as a term of their employment, without specifying the details.

chunks.en: When he came to his father,
chunks.st: And when he came back to his father and reported what he had done, Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Matya

chunks.en: his father said to him,
chunks.st: said to him:

chunks.he: בְּנִי, אֲפִלּוּ אִם אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה לָהֶם
chunks.en: "My son, even if you make for them
chunks.st: My son, even if you were to prepare a feast for them

chunks.en: a meal like Shlomo HaMelech's in his time,
chunks.st: like that of King Solomon in his time,

chunks.en: you have not done your duty to them,
chunks.st: you would not have fulfilled your obligation to them,

chunks.en: because they are children of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov.
chunks.st: as they are the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

chunks.en: Rather, before they start working,
chunks.st: Rather, before they begin engaging in their labor,

chunks.en: go out and tell them,
chunks.st: go out and say to them:

chunks.en: 'This is on condition that you can ask me
chunks.st: The stipulation that food will be provided is on the condition that you have the right to claim from me

chunks.en: only for bread and beans.'"
chunks.explain: That was the usual meal for workers.
chunks.st: only a meal of bread and legumes, which is the typical meal given to laborers.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Matya’s son

chunks.en: he did not need to say it;
chunks.st: did not need to state this condition, as the principle is that

chunks.en: everything follows the custom of the place.
chunks.st: everything is in accordance with the regional custom.

mishnayos.summary: The Torah lets a worker eat from the food he works with, but only at certain times: when picking it at the end of its growing, or while working on it before it is finished. He may not eat from things that do not grow from the ground.

chunks.en: And these workers may eat by Torah law:
chunks.st: And these laborers may eat by Torah law:

chunks.en: one who works with food attached to the ground
chunks.st: A laborer who works with produce attached to the ground

chunks.en: when its work is being finished,
chunks.explain: Like picking ripe grapes.
chunks.st: at the time of the completion of its work, e.g., harvesting produce;

chunks.en: and with food picked from the ground
chunks.st: and a laborer who works with produce detached from the ground

chunks.en: before its work is finished,
chunks.st: before the completion of its work,
chunks.stMore: i.e., before it is sufficiently processed and thereby subject to tithes.

chunks.en: with something that grows from the ground.
chunks.st: And this is the halakha provided that they are working with an item whose growth is from the land.

chunks.en: And these may not eat:
chunks.st: And these are laborers who may not eat:

chunks.en: one who works with food attached to the ground
chunks.st: A laborer who works with produce attached to the ground

chunks.en: when it is not yet finished,
chunks.explain: It is still growing.
chunks.st: not at the time of the completion of its work, i.e., while it is still growing;

chunks.he: וּבְתָלוּשׁ מִן הַקַּרְקַע מֵאַחַר שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ,
chunks.en: and with picked food after its work is finished,
chunks.st: and a laborer who works with produce detached from the ground after the completion of its work, when it is sufficiently processed and therefore subject to tithes;

chunks.en: and with something that does not grow from the ground.
chunks.st: and a laborer who works with an item whose growth is not from the land.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna details the halakha that a laborer is permitted to eat from the produce with which he is working.

mishnayos.summary: A worker may eat even if he works with only his hands, only his feet, or his shoulder. Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says he must work with both his hands and his feet.

chunks.he: הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה בְיָדָיו אֲבָל לֹא בְרַגְלָיו,
chunks.en: If he worked with his hands but not his feet,
chunks.st: If a laborer was performing labor with his hands but not with his feet,

chunks.en: or with his feet but not his hands,
chunks.st: or with his feet but not with his hands, e.g., pressing grapes,

chunks.en: even with his shoulder,
chunks.st: or even if he was performing labor only with his shoulder,

chunks.en: he may eat.
chunks.st: this one may eat the produce of the field.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

chunks.en: only when he works with his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: A laborer may not eat unless he performs labor with his hands and with his feet.

mishnayos.summary: A worker may eat only the kind of fruit he is working with, and he may wait to eat from the best ones. He eats while working, and also while walking between rows and coming back from the winepress.

chunks.en: If he was working with figs,
chunks.st: If a laborer was performing labor with figs

chunks.en: he may not eat grapes;
chunks.st: he may not eat grapes;

chunks.en: with grapes, he may not eat figs.
chunks.st: if he was performing labor with grapes he may not eat figs,
chunks.stMore: as he may eat only the type of food with which he is working. This is the halakha even if he was employed to perform labor with both types of produce but is currently performing labor with only one of them.

chunks.en: But he may hold himself back
chunks.st: But he may hold himself back from eating

chunks.en: until he reaches the good ones, and then eat.
chunks.st: until he reaches a place of good-quality grapes or figs and eat from these, as they are the same type of food.

chunks.he: וְכֻלָּן לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה,
chunks.en: And for all of them, they said only while working.
chunks.st: And with regard to all of these cases the Sages said that he may eat only at the time of work.

chunks.he: אֲבָל מִשּׁוּם הָשֵׁב אֲבֵדָה לַבְּעָלִים אָמְרוּ,
chunks.en: But so that the owner does not lose out, they said,
chunks.explain: So the workers will not stop working to eat.
chunks.st: But due to the obligation to restore lost property to its owners, i.e., so that workers would not neglect their task, they said that

chunks.en: workers may eat while walking from row to row,
chunks.st: laborers may eat as they walk from one row of a vineyard or plantation to another row,

chunks.en: and coming back from the winepress.
chunks.st: and upon their return from the winepress.

chunks.en: And a donkey, while it is being unloaded.
chunks.st: And with regard to a donkey, it is permitted to eat when it is being unloaded. This statement will be explained in the Gemara.

mishnayos.summary: A worker may eat even a lot of cucumbers or dates. Rabbi Elazar Chisma says not more than his pay; the Sages allow it, but teach a person not to eat too much so he will still get hired.

chunks.en: A worker may eat cucumbers, even a dinar's worth,
chunks.st: A laborer may eat cucumbers while he works, and this is the halakha even if the amount he eats is equal in value to a dinar;

chunks.en: and dates, even a dinar's worth.
chunks.st: or he may eat dates, and this is the halakha even if the amount he eats is equal in value to a dinar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar Chisma says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar Ḥisma says:

chunks.he: לֹא יֹאכַל פּוֹעֵל יָתֵר עַל שְׂכָרוֹ.
chunks.en: a worker may not eat more than his pay.
chunks.st: A laborer may not eat more than the value of his wages,

chunks.en: But the Sages allow it.
chunks.st: but the Rabbis permit it, according to the strict letter of the law.

chunks.en: But we teach a person
chunks.st: But one teaches a person

chunks.en: not to eat too much,
chunks.st: not to be a glutton

chunks.en: and close the door in his own face.
chunks.explain: People will not want to hire him.
chunks.st: and thereby close the opening to other job offers in his face. When people hear of his greed they will be reluctant to hire him.

mishnayos.summary: A worker may agree to get extra pay instead of eating, and a man may agree to this for his grown children, servants and wife, who understand. He may not agree for young children, young servants or his animal.

chunks.en: A person may make a deal for himself,
chunks.explain: To get more pay instead of eating.
chunks.st: A man can stipulate on his own behalf
chunks.stMore: that he receive a certain increase in his wages instead of eating the produce with which he works, and similarly, he can stipulate this

chunks.en: for his grown son and daughter,
chunks.st: on behalf of his adult son or daughter,

chunks.en: for his grown servant and maid,
chunks.st: on behalf of his adult Canaanite slave or Canaanite maidservant,

chunks.en: for his wife,
chunks.st: or on behalf of his wife, with their agreement,

chunks.en: because they understand.
chunks.st: because they have the basic level of mental competence, i.e., they are legally competent and can therefore waive their rights.

chunks.en: But he may not make the deal
chunks.st: But he cannot stipulate this

chunks.en: for his young son and daughter,
chunks.st: on behalf of his minor son or daughter,

chunks.he: וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הַקְּטַנִּים,
chunks.en: or for his young servant and maid,
chunks.st: nor on behalf of his minor Canaanite slave or Canaanite maidservant,

chunks.en: or for his animal,
chunks.st: nor on behalf of his animal,

chunks.en: because they do not understand.
chunks.st: as they do not have the basic level of mental competence.

mishnayos.summary: Workers may not eat fourth-year fruit or food that was already finished for ma'aser. If the owner did not tell them, he must make the food permitted and feed them.

chunks.en: If someone hires workers to work
chunks.st: In the case of one who hires a laborer to perform labor

chunks.en: with his fourth-year fruit,
chunks.explain: Fruit in a tree's fourth year is holy, like ma'aser sheni.
chunks.st: with his fourth-year fruit,

chunks.en: they may not eat.
chunks.st: such laborers may not eat the fruit.

chunks.en: If he did not tell them,
chunks.st: And if he did not inform them beforehand that they were working with fourth-year fruit,

chunks.en: he redeems it and feeds them.
chunks.st: he must redeem the fruit and feed them.

chunks.en: If his fig cakes broke apart,
chunks.st: If his fig cakes broke apart and crumbled, so that they must be preserved again,

chunks.en: or his barrels opened,
chunks.st: or if his barrels of wine opened and he hired workers to reseal them,

chunks.en: they may not eat.
chunks.explain: Their work was already finished, so ma'aser must be taken first.
chunks.st: these laborers may not eat,
chunks.stMore: as the work of the figs or wine had already been completed with regard to tithes, from which point a laborer may not eat them.

chunks.en: If he did not tell them,
chunks.st: And if he did not inform them, he

chunks.en: he takes ma'aser and feeds them.
chunks.st: must tithe the food and feed them.

mishnayos.summary: Fruit watchmen may eat by local custom. There are four kinds of watchmen, and the mishnah teaches when each one swears and when each one must pay.

chunks.en: Fruit watchmen may eat by the custom of the place,
chunks.st: Watchmen of produce may eat the produce of the field or vineyard by local regulations,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in accordance with the ordinances accepted by the residents of that place,

chunks.en: but not by Torah law.
chunks.st: but not by Torah law.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of watchmen:
chunks.st: There are four types of bailees, to whom different halakhot apply. They are as follows:

chunks.en: a free watchman, and a borrower,
chunks.st: An unpaid bailee, who receives no compensation for safeguarding the item; and the borrower of an item for his own use;

chunks.en: a paid watchman, and a renter.
chunks.st: a paid bailee, who is provided with a salary for watching over an item; and a renter,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a bailee who pays a fee for the use of a vessel or animal. If the item was stolen, lost, or broken, or if the animal died in any manner, their halakhot are as follows:

chunks.en: A free watchman swears about everything.
chunks.explain: He swears he was not careless, and does not pay.
chunks.st: An unpaid bailee takes an oath over every
chunks.stMore: outcome; whether the item was lost, stolen, or broken, or if the animal died, the unpaid bailee must take an oath that it happened as he described, and he is then exempt from payment.

chunks.en: The borrower pays for everything.
chunks.st: The borrower does not take an oath, but pays for every outcome, even in a circumstance beyond his control.

chunks.en: A paid watchman and a renter
chunks.st: And the halakhot of a paid bailee and a renter are the same:

chunks.en: swear about an animal that broke a leg,
chunks.st: They take an oath over an injured animal,

chunks.en: or was captured, or died,
chunks.st: over a captured animal, and over a dead
chunks.stMore: animal, attesting that the mishaps were caused by circumstances beyond their control, and they are exempt,

chunks.en: and pay for what was lost or stolen.
chunks.st: but they must pay for loss or theft.

mishnayos.summary: A paid watchman does not pay for something he could not stop, like two wolves, robbers or wild animals. But if he took the animals to a dangerous place, he must pay.

chunks.en: One wolf
chunks.st: One wolf that approaches a flock and attacks

chunks.en: is not something he could not stop.
chunks.explain: The shepherd can chase one wolf away.
chunks.st: is not considered a circumstance beyond one’s control, as the shepherd can drive it away,

chunks.en: Two wolves are something he could not stop.
chunks.st: but an attack by two wolves is considered a circumstance beyond one’s control.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: when wolves are attacking everywhere,
chunks.st: At a time of wolf attacks,
chunks.stMore: when many wolves come out of hiding and pounce on animals at every corner,

chunks.en: even one wolf is something he could not stop.
chunks.st: even an attack by one wolf is considered a circumstance beyond one’s control.

chunks.en: Two dogs
chunks.st: An attack by two dogs

chunks.en: are not something he could not stop.
chunks.st: is not considered a circumstance beyond one’s control.

chunks.he: יַדּוּעַ הַבַּבְלִי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
chunks.en: Yadua HaBavli says in the name of Rabbi Meir,
chunks.st: Yadua the Babylonian says in the name of Rabbi Meir:

chunks.en: From one side,
chunks.st: If the two dogs came and attacked from one direction

chunks.en: it is not something he could not stop;
chunks.st: it is not considered a circumstance beyond one’s control,

chunks.en: from two sides, it is something he could not stop.
chunks.st: but if they attacked from two directions, this is considered a circumstance beyond one’s control, as the shepherd cannot protect his flock from both of them at once.

chunks.en: Robbers are something he could not stop.
chunks.st: If bandits came, this is considered a circumstance beyond one’s control.

chunks.en: A lion, a bear, a leopard, a cheetah and a snake
chunks.st: Likewise, with regard to an attack by a lion, a bear, a leopard, a cheetah, and a snake,

chunks.en: are something he could not stop.
chunks.st: these are each considered a circumstance beyond one’s control.

chunks.en: When? When they came by themselves.
chunks.st: When is an attack by one of the above considered beyond his control, which means that a paid bailee is exempt? It is when the dangerous beasts or bandits came of their own accord to the usual grazing spot.

chunks.en: But if he took them
chunks.st: But if the shepherd led his flock

chunks.en: to a place of wild animal packs and robbers,
chunks.st: to a place of groups of beasts or bandits,

chunks.en: it is not something he could not stop.
chunks.st: this is not considered a circumstance beyond one’s control, as he is at fault.

mishnayos.summary: If an animal died by itself or fell on its own, the watchman could not stop it; if he hurt it or brought it up a cliff, he is at fault. Watchmen may also make a deal to be free from swearing or paying.

chunks.en: If it died the normal way,
chunks.st: If the animal died in its normal manner,

chunks.en: that is something he could not stop.
chunks.st: this is considered a circumstance beyond one’s control;

chunks.en: If he made it suffer and it died,
chunks.st: if he afflicted it by overworking it or by negligent treatment and it died,

chunks.en: that is not something he could not stop.
chunks.st: this is not considered a circumstance beyond one’s control.

chunks.en: If it climbed to the tops of cliffs and fell and died,
chunks.st: If the animal ascended to the top of a cliff and fell down and died,

chunks.en: that is something he could not stop.
chunks.st: this is considered a circumstance beyond one’s control.

chunks.en: If he brought it up to the tops of cliffs and it fell and died,
chunks.st: If the shepherd himself brought it up to the top of a cliff and it fell down and died,

chunks.en: that is not something he could not stop.
chunks.st: this is not considered a circumstance beyond one’s control.
chunks.stMore: The halakhot of bailees stated in the previous mishna apply to standard cases. The halakha is that in any case involving monetary matters the parties may agree to special terms.

chunks.he: מַתְנֶה שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם לִהְיוֹת פָּטוּר מִשְּׁבוּעָה,
chunks.en: A free watchman may make a deal not to have to swear,
chunks.st: Therefore, an unpaid bailee may stipulate with the owner that he will be exempt from taking an oath if the item is lost,

chunks.en: and a borrower not to have to pay,
chunks.st: and similarly, a borrower may stipulate that he will be exempt from having to pay,

chunks.en: a paid watchman and a renter
chunks.st: and a paid bailee or a renter

chunks.en: not to have to swear or pay.
chunks.st: can stipulate that he will be exempt from taking an oath and from having to pay, as one can relinquish his monetary rights.

mishnayos.summary: A condition that goes against the Torah does not work. A condition must be said before the deal, not after it, and then it counts.

chunks.he: כָּל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה,
chunks.en: Anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah,
chunks.st: anyone who stipulates counter to that which is written in the Torah,

chunks.en: his condition does not count.
chunks.st: his stipulation is void.

chunks.en: And any condition that has the action first,
chunks.st: And any condition that is preceded by an action,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the agreement is formulated with the promise of an action followed by a statement that this action will be carried out only under certain terms,

chunks.en: that condition does not count.
chunks.explain: The condition must be said before the deal.
chunks.st: the condition is void
chunks.stMore: and the promise remains intact. The condition must be stated before the action.

chunks.en: And any condition he can keep at the end,
chunks.st: And with regard to any condition that one can ultimately fulfill,

chunks.en: and he said it at the start,
chunks.st: but he stipulated with him initially,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in practice the action is performed first, followed by the fulfillment of the condition, nevertheless, because it was formulated in the proper manner, with the condition first,

chunks.en: that condition counts.
chunks.st: his condition is valid.
chunks.stMore: If the condition cannot be fulfilled at all, once the action has been carried out the condition is void.

mishnayos.stIntro: With regard to matters that do not involve monetary claims,

mishnayos.summary: A borrower does not pay for a borrowed cow that died if he also borrowed or hired its owner first, because the Torah says "if its owner is with him, he does not pay." If he borrowed the cow first, he pays.

chunks.en: If someone borrows a cow
chunks.st: In the case of one who borrowed a cow

chunks.en: and borrowed its owner with it,
chunks.explain: The owner works for him for free.
chunks.st: and borrowed the services of its owner with it,

chunks.en: or hired its owner with it,
chunks.st: or he borrowed a cow and hired its owner with it,

chunks.en: or he borrowed or hired the owner
chunks.st: or he borrowed the services of the owner or hired him

chunks.en: and after that borrowed the cow,
chunks.st: and afterward borrowed the cow;

chunks.en: and it died, he does not pay,
chunks.st: in all such cases, if the cow died, the borrower is exempt
chunks.stMore: from liability. Although a borrower is generally liable to pay if a cow he borrowed dies, here he is exempt,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "If its owner is with him, he does not pay."
chunks.st: “If its owner is with him, he does not pay” (Exodus 22:14).

chunks.en: But if he borrowed the cow
chunks.st: But if one first borrowed the cow

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁאַל אֶת הַבְּעָלִים אוֹ שְׂכָרָן,
chunks.en: and after that borrowed or hired the owner,
chunks.st: and only afterward borrowed the services of the owner or hired him,

chunks.en: and it died, he must pay,
chunks.st: and the cow died, he is liable
chunks.stMore: to pay the owner for the cow. This is the halakha even if the owner was working for the borrower at the time,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "If its owner is not with him, he must surely pay."
chunks.st: “If its owner is not with him, he shall pay” (Exodus 22:13).

mishnayos.summary: A cow was partly borrowed and partly rented, and it died, and nobody is sure in which part of the time. The mishnah teaches who pays when each side is sure or not sure.

chunks.en: If someone borrows a cow:
chunks.st: There is one who borrowed a cow.

chunks.he: שְׁאָלָהּ חֲצִי הַיּוֹם וּשְׂכָרָהּ חֲצִי הַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: he borrowed it half the day and rented it half the day,
chunks.st: He borrowed it for half of the day and rented it for the other half of the day;

chunks.en: or borrowed it today and rented it tomorrow,
chunks.st: or he borrowed it for today and rented it for tomorrow;

chunks.en: or rented one cow and borrowed one,
chunks.st: or he rented one cow and borrowed another one from the same person.

chunks.en: and it died.
chunks.explain: A borrower pays if it dies; a renter does not.
chunks.st: And in one of the first two cases, the cow died
chunks.stMore: and it is not clear during which period the cow died. Or in the last case, one of the cows died and it is not clear whether it had been the borrowed cow or the rented cow.

chunks.en: If the lender says, "The borrowed one died,"
chunks.st: If the lender then says: The borrowed cow is the one that died;

chunks.en: "It died on the day it was borrowed,"
chunks.st: or: It died on the day that it was being borrowed;

chunks.en: "It died at the time it was borrowed,"
chunks.st: or: It died during the period in which it was being borrowed,
chunks.stMore: so that, according to his claim, the borrower is liable to pay for the cow,

chunks.en: and the other says, "I do not know," he must pay.
chunks.st: and the other one, the borrower, says: I do not know what happened, the borrower is liable to pay.

chunks.en: If the renter says, "The rented one died,"
chunks.st: If the renter says: The rented cow is the one that died;

chunks.en: "It died on the day it was rented,"
chunks.st: or: It died on the day that it was being rented;

chunks.en: "It died at the time it was rented,"
chunks.st: or: It died during the period in which it was being rented,

chunks.en: and the other says, "I do not know," he does not pay.
chunks.st: and the other one, the owner of the cow, says: I do not know what happened, the renter is exempt.

chunks.he: זֶה אוֹמֵר שְׁאוּלָה וְזֶה אוֹמֵר שְׂכוּרָה,
chunks.en: If one says "borrowed" and one says "rented,"
chunks.st: If this owner says with certitude: The borrowed cow is the one that died, and that renter says with certitude: The rented cow is the one that died,

chunks.en: the renter swears that the rented one died.
chunks.st: then the renter takes an oath that the rented cow is the one that died, and he is then exempt from liability.

chunks.en: If this one says, "I do not know,"
chunks.st: If this one says: I do not know what happened,

chunks.en: and that one says, "I do not know," they split it.
chunks.st: and that one says: I do not know what happened, then they divide
chunks.stMore: the disputed amount. The bailee is liable to pay for only half the value of the cow.

mishnayos.summary: A borrowed cow that dies on the way to the borrower is not yet his responsibility. But if the borrower agreed to have it sent with a certain person, he pays from when that person takes it, and the same when he returns it.

chunks.en: If someone borrows a cow,
chunks.st: In the case of one who borrowed a cow,

chunks.en: and the owner sent it to him with his son,
chunks.st: and the lender sent it to the borrower by the hand of his son,

chunks.en: with his servant, with his messenger,
chunks.st: or by the hand of his slave, or by the hand of his agent,

chunks.en: or with the borrower's son, with his servant,
chunks.st: or by the hand of the borrower’s son, or by the hand of his slave,

chunks.en: or with the borrower's messenger,
chunks.st: or by the hand of the agent of the borrower;

chunks.en: and it died, he does not pay.
chunks.explain: It did not reach the borrower yet.
chunks.st: and it died on the way, the borrower is exempt,
chunks.stMore: because the period of borrowing begins only once the cow reaches his domain.

chunks.en: If the borrower said to him,
chunks.st: The borrower said to the lender:

chunks.en: "Send it to me with my son,
chunks.st: Send it to me by the hand of my son,

chunks.en: with my servant, with my messenger,
chunks.st: or by the hand of my slave, or by the hand of my agent,

chunks.en: or with your son, with your servant,
chunks.st: or by the hand of your son, or by the hand of your slave,

chunks.en: with your messenger,"
chunks.st: or by the hand of your agent.

chunks.en: or if the lender said to him,
chunks.st: Or, in a case where the lender said explicitly to the borrower:

chunks.en: "I am sending it to you with my son,
chunks.st: I am sending it to you by the hand of my son,

chunks.en: with my servant, with my messenger,
chunks.st: or by the hand of my slave, or by the hand of my agent,

chunks.he: אוֹ בְּיַד בִּנְךָ, בְּיַד עַבְדְּךָ, בְּיַד שְׁלוּחֲךָ,
chunks.en: or with your son, with your servant, with your messenger,"
chunks.st: or by the hand of your son, or by the hand of your slave, or by the hand of your agent;

chunks.en: and the borrower said to him,
chunks.st: and the borrower said to him:

chunks.he: שַׁלַּח, וְשִׁלְּחָהּ וָמֵתָה, חַיָּב. וְכֵן בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמַּחֲזִירָהּ:
chunks.en: "Send it," and he sent it and it died, he must pay. And the same when he returns it.
chunks.st: Send it as you have said, and he then sent it, and it died on the way, then the borrower is liable
chunks.stMore: to pay the lender the value of his cow. Since the borrower agreed to the cow’s being brought to him by the hand of another, he bears liability from the moment the cow was transferred into that person’s possession.

mishnayos.summary: When it is not known if a baby animal or child was born before or after a sale, the buyer and seller split it. When it is not known which of two servants or fields was sold, the mishnah teaches who wins.

chunks.en: If someone trades a cow for a donkey and it gave birth,
chunks.st: With regard to one who exchanges a cow for a donkey, such that by virtue of the cow owner’s act of acquisition on the donkey, the donkey’s erstwhile owner simultaneously acquires the cow, wherever it happens to be located, and afterward the cow is found to have calved;

chunks.en: and the same if someone sells his maidservant and she had a baby,
chunks.st: and similarly, with regard to one who sells his Canaanite maidservant, with the acquisition effected by the buyer giving him money, and afterward she is found to have given birth
chunks.stMore: to a child, who will be a slave belonging to his mother’s master, at times it is uncertain whether the offspring was born before or after the transaction.

chunks.en: this one says, "Before I sold,"
chunks.st: If this seller says: The birth occurred before I sold the cow or maidservant, and so the offspring belongs to me,

chunks.en: and that one says, "After I bought," they split it.
chunks.st: and that buyer says: The birth occurred after I purchased the cow or maidservant, and so the offspring belongs to me, they divide
chunks.stMore: the value of the offspring between them. The mishna continues: There is a case of

chunks.en: If he had two servants,
chunks.st: one who had two Canaanite slaves,

chunks.en: one big and one small,
chunks.st: one large, worth more on the slave market, and one small, worth less on the slave market,

chunks.en: or two fields,
chunks.st: and similarly, one who had two fields,

chunks.en: one big and one small,
chunks.explain: He sold one and they argue which one.
chunks.st: one large and one small.
chunks.stMore: He sold one of them, and there was a dispute between the buyer and the seller concerning which one was sold.

chunks.en: if the buyer says, "I bought the big one,"
chunks.st: If the buyer says: I purchased the large one,

chunks.en: and the other says, "I do not know,"
chunks.st: and the other one, i.e., the seller, says: I do not know which I sold;

chunks.en: he gets the big one.
chunks.st: the buyer is entitled to take the large one.

chunks.en: If the seller says, "I sold the small one,"
chunks.st: If the seller says: I sold the small one,

chunks.en: and the other says, "I do not know,"
chunks.st: and the other one, i.e., the buyer, says: I do not know which one I purchased;

chunks.en: he gets only the small one.
chunks.st: the buyer is entitled to take only the small one.

chunks.he: זֶה אוֹמֵר גָּדוֹל וְזֶה אוֹמֵר קָטָן,
chunks.en: If this one says "big" and that one says "small,"
chunks.st: If this one says: The large one was sold, and that one says: The small one was sold,

chunks.en: the seller swears that he sold the small one.
chunks.st: then the seller takes an oath that it was the small one that he sold, and then the buyer takes the small one.

chunks.en: If this one says, "I do not know,"
chunks.st: If this one says: I do not know which one was sold,

chunks.en: and that one says, "I do not know," they split it.
chunks.st: and that one says: I do not know which one was sold, they divide the disputed amount between them.

mishnayos.summary: Someone sold olive trees for wood, and they grew olives before being cut down. If the olives are poor, the buyer keeps them; if good, buyer and seller split them. The same if a river carried trees into someone else's field.

chunks.en: If someone sells his olive trees for wood,
chunks.st: In the case of one who sells his olive trees to another so he can chop them down and use them for their wood,

chunks.en: and they grew olives that make less than a revi'is of oil for a se'ah,
chunks.st: and before he chopped them down they yielded olives, if the olives are of a quality that could provide the value of less than a quarter-log of oil per se’a of olives,

chunks.en: the olives belong to the owner of the trees.
chunks.st: these olives are the property of the new owner of the olive trees, i.e., the buyer.

chunks.en: If they made a revi'is for a se'ah,
chunks.st: If they yielded olives that could provide the value of a quarter-log or more of oil per se’a of olives,

chunks.en: this one says, "My trees grew them,"
chunks.st: and this one, the buyer, says: My olive trees yielded the olives and so I have a right to them,

chunks.en: and that one says, "My land grew them," they split them.
chunks.st: and that one, the seller, says: The nourishment from my land yielded the olives and so I have a right to them, then they divide the olives between them.

chunks.en: If a river washed away his olive trees
chunks.st: In the event that a river swept away one’s olive trees

chunks.en: and put them into his friend's field,
chunks.explain: And they took root there and grew olives.
chunks.st: and deposited them in the field of another, and they took root there and yielded olives,

chunks.en: this one says, "My trees grew them,"
chunks.st: this one, i.e., the owner of the trees, says: My olive trees yielded the olives and so I have a right to them,

chunks.en: and that one says, "My land grew them," they split them.
chunks.st: and that one, i.e., the owner of the field, says: The nourishment from my land yielded the olives and so I have a right to them, then they divide the olives between them.

mishnayos.summary: A landlord who rents out a house must give the renter time before making him leave. How long depends on the season, whether it is a city, and whether it is a store.

chunks.en: If someone rents a house to his friend
chunks.st: In the case of one who rents out a house in a town to another

chunks.en: in the rainy season,
chunks.st: in the rainy season,

chunks.en: he cannot make him leave
chunks.st: the owner cannot evict the renter from the house

chunks.en: from Sukkos until Pesach.
chunks.st: from the festival of Sukkot until Passover.

chunks.en: In the summer,
chunks.st: If the rental was in the summer,

chunks.en: thirty days.
chunks.explain: He must tell him thirty days before.
chunks.st: he must give thirty days’ notice before he can evict him.

chunks.he: וּבַכְּרַכִּים, אֶחָד יְמוֹת הַחַמָּה וְאֶחָד יְמוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים,
chunks.en: In big cities, both in summer and in the rainy season,
chunks.st: And for a house located in the cities [uvakerakim], both in the summer and in the rainy season

chunks.en: twelve months.
chunks.st: he must give twelve months’ notice.

chunks.en: For stores, both in towns and in cities,
chunks.st: And for shops that he rented out, both in towns and in cities,

chunks.en: twelve months.
chunks.st: he must give twelve months’ notice.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: a bakers' or dyers' shop,
chunks.st: For a baker’s shop or a dyer’s shop,

chunks.en: three years.
chunks.st: one must give three years’ notice.

mishnayos.summary: A landlord must give the door, the bolt, the lock and anything a craftsman must make. The renter makes simple things himself. The manure in the yard belongs to the landlord, and the renter gets only the ashes from the oven.

chunks.en: If someone rents a house to his friend,
chunks.st: If one rents out a house to another,

chunks.en: the landlord must give the door,
chunks.st: the landlord bears the responsibility for providing the door,

chunks.en: the bolt, and the lock,
chunks.st: for providing the bolt, for providing the lock,

chunks.en: and anything that is a craftsman's work.
chunks.st: and for providing every item in the house that is essential for normal living and requires the work of a craftsman to provide it.

chunks.en: But something that is not a craftsman's work,
chunks.st: But with regard to an item that does not require the work of a craftsman,

chunks.en: the renter makes it.
chunks.st: the renter is responsible to make it.

chunks.en: The manure belongs to the landlord,
chunks.st: The manure found in the courtyard of a rented house is the property of the landlord,

chunks.en: and the renter gets only what comes out
chunks.st: and the renter has rights only to the ashes

chunks.en: of the oven and the stove.
chunks.explain: The ashes, which also help fields grow.
chunks.st: that come out of the oven and the stove, which can also be used as a fertilizer.

mishnayos.summary: In a leap year with an extra month, whether the renter pays for it depends on whether the rent was set by the year or by the month. When both were said, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and Rabbi Yosei said to split it.

chunks.en: If someone rents a house to his friend for a year,
chunks.st: In the case of one who rents out a house to another for a year

chunks.en: and the year got an extra month,
chunks.explain: A Jewish leap year has thirteen months.
chunks.st: and then the year was intercalated, adding an additional month to that year,

chunks.en: the extra month goes to the renter.
chunks.explain: He pays nothing more.
chunks.st: the fact that it was intercalated is to the benefit of the renter.
chunks.stMore: Since the rental was defined in terms of a year, the additional month is automatically included, and the renter need not pay additional rent for it.

chunks.en: If he rented it to him by the month,
chunks.st: If a landlord rented out a house to another for a year, with the price set as a certain sum for each of the months,

chunks.en: and the year got an extra month,
chunks.st: and then the year was intercalated,

chunks.en: the extra month goes to the landlord.
chunks.st: the fact that it was intercalated is to the benefit of the landlord.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְצִפּוֹרִי בְּאֶחָד שֶׁשָּׂכַר מֶרְחָץ מֵחֲבֵרוֹ
chunks.en: There was a story in Tzippori with one who rented a bathhouse from his friend
chunks.st: An incident occurred in Tzippori involving one who rented a bathhouse from another

chunks.en: for twelve gold coins a year,
chunks.st: where they stated that the rent would be: Twelve gold dinars per year,

chunks.en: a gold dinar a month.
chunks.st: a gold dinar per month, and then the year was intercalated.

chunks.he: וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
chunks.en: The story came before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
