mishnayos.summary: If a rented house falls down, the landlord must give the renter another house just like it, not bigger or smaller and with the same windows, unless both agree.

chunks.en: If someone rents a house to his friend and it fell,
chunks.st: In the case of one who rented out a house to another, and then the house fell,

chunks.en: he must give him a house.
chunks.st: the landlord is obligated to provide the renter with another house.

chunks.en: If it was small,
chunks.st: If the original house was small,

chunks.en: he should not make it big;
chunks.st: the landlord may not construct a large house as a replacement,

chunks.en: big, he should not make it small.
chunks.st: and if the original was large, he may not construct a small house as a replacement.

chunks.en: One room, he should not make it two;
chunks.st: If the original had one room, he may not construct the replacement with two rooms,

chunks.en: two, he should not make it one.
chunks.st: and if the original had two rooms, he may not construct the replacement with one.

chunks.he: לֹא יִפְחֹת מֵהַחַלּוֹנוֹת וְלֹא יוֹסִיף עֲלֵיהֶן,
chunks.en: He should not take away windows or add to them,
chunks.st: He may not reduce the number of windows, nor add to them,

chunks.en: unless both of them agree.
chunks.st: except with the agreement of both of them.

mishnayos.summary: A farmer who takes a field to work for its owner must follow the local custom about cutting, pulling up and plowing. He and the owner share the straw and the vine branches just as they share the crop, and both give the poles.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend to farm,
chunks.explain: He works it and pays the owner with some of the crop.
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives a field from another
chunks.stMore: to cultivate, either as a tenant farmer, who, in exchange for the right to farm the land, gives a set amount of the produce to the owner, or as a sharecropper, who cultivates the land and receives a set proportion of the produce, the halakha is as follows:

chunks.en: where people usually cut the crop, he cuts it;
chunks.st: In a location where those cultivating the land were accustomed to cut the produce, this one must cut it as well.

chunks.en: to pull it up, he pulls it up;
chunks.st: In a location where they were accustomed to uproot the produce, not to cut it with a sickle or a scythe, this one must uproot it as well.

chunks.en: to plow after it, he plows.
chunks.st: If they were accustomed to plow the land after harvesting the produce, this one must plow as well.

chunks.en: Everything follows the custom of the place.
chunks.st: All farming of the land shall be conducted in accordance with regional custom.

chunks.en: Just as they split the grain,
chunks.st: Just as the halakha is that the owner of the field and the one cultivating it divide the produce,

chunks.en: so they split the straw and stubble.
chunks.st: so too the halakha is that they divide the stubble and the straw.

chunks.en: Just as they split the wine,
chunks.st: Just as the halakha is that the owner of the field and the one cultivating it divide the wine,

chunks.en: so they split the vine branches and the poles.
chunks.st: so too the halakha is that they divide the branches pruned from the vines and the poles.

chunks.en: And both of them give the poles.
chunks.explain: The poles hold up the grapevines.
chunks.st: And the two of them, i.e., the landowner and the one cultivating the field, both supply the poles.

mishnayos.summary: If a farmer took a watered field or a field of trees, and the spring dried up or the trees were cut down, he pays the full rent. But if he named the spring or trees in the deal, he may pay less.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend to farm,
chunks.st: In the case of one who receives a field from another to cultivate

chunks.he: וְהִיא בֵית הַשְּׁלָחִין אוֹ בֵית הָאִילָן,
chunks.en: and it is a watered field or a field of trees,
chunks.st: and it is an irrigated field or a field with trees,

chunks.en: and the spring dried up or the trees were cut down,
chunks.st: if the spring that irrigated the field dried up or the trees were cut down,

chunks.en: he does not take anything off his rent.
chunks.st: he does not subtract from the produce he owes the owner as part of his tenancy,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he presumably considered these factors when agreeing to cultivate the field.

chunks.en: But if he said to him,
chunks.st: But if the cultivator said to the landowner explicitly:

chunks.he: חֲכֹר לִי שְׂדֵה בֵית הַשְּׁלָחִין זֶה
chunks.en: "Rent me this watered field,"
chunks.st: Lease me this irrigated field,

chunks.en: or "this field of trees,"
chunks.st: or he said: Lease me this field with trees,

chunks.en: and the spring dried up or the trees were cut down,
chunks.st: and the spring dried up or the trees were cut down,

chunks.en: he takes it off his rent.
chunks.st: he may subtract from the produce he owes as part of his tenancy.

mishnayos.summary: A farmer who left the field he took unplanted must pay the owner what it could have grown, because the contract says so.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend and leaves it unplanted,
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives a field from another as a contractor and then lets it lie fallow and does not work the land at all,

chunks.en: they estimate it,
chunks.st: the court appraises it by evaluating

chunks.en: how much it could have grown,
chunks.st: how much it was able to produce if cultivated,

chunks.en: and he gives it to him,
chunks.st: and he gives his share of this amount to the owner.

chunks.en: because this is what he writes to him:
chunks.st: The reason is that this is what a cultivator writes to the owner in a standard contract:

chunks.en: "If I leave it unplanted and do not work it,
chunks.st: If I let the field lie fallow and do not cultivate it,

chunks.en: I will pay with the best."
chunks.st: I will pay with best-quality produce.

mishnayos.summary: A farmer who does not want to weed the field cannot say it is not the owner's business. The owner can say that after he leaves, the weeds will stay.

chunks.he: הַמְקַבֵּל שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵרוֹ וְלֹא רָצָה לְנַכֵּשׁ,
chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend and did not want to weed it,
chunks.st: With regard to one who received a field from another to cultivate and did not want to weed it,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "What do you care,
chunks.st: and he then said to the owner: What do you care if I neglect the land? You will not suffer a loss

chunks.en: since I give you your rent?"
chunks.st: since I will give you the amount of produce I owe you for your granting me tenancy, regardless of the state of the field.

chunks.en: We do not listen to him,
chunks.st: Nevertheless, they do not listen to him.

chunks.en: because the owner can say to him,
chunks.st: The reason is because the owner of the land can say to him:

chunks.en: "Tomorrow you leave it,
chunks.st: Tomorrow you will depart from the field,

chunks.en: and it will grow weeds for me."
chunks.st: and it will grow weeds for me,
chunks.stMore: which will remain there and disrupt the yield of the field for years to come.

mishnayos.summary: A farmer must keep working a field that grows only a little, as long as there is enough for a pile. Rabbi Yehuda says it is enough if it grows as much as the seeds that were planted.

chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend and it did not grow much,
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives a field from another to cultivate and it did not produce a sufficient crop to cover the expenses of its upkeep,

chunks.he: אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהַעֲמִיד כְּרִי,
chunks.en: if it has enough to make a pile,
chunks.st: if it has enough produce to form a pile

chunks.en: he must keep working it.
chunks.st: he is obligated to take care of it and give the owner his share.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: "What size is a pile?
chunks.explain: Fields are different sizes.
chunks.st: What fixed measure is a pile?
chunks.stMore: There is no inherent measure of produce that is considered significant, as it all depends on the size of the plot of land in question.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ כְּדֵי נְפִילָה:
chunks.en: Rather, if it has as much as the seeds that were planted."
chunks.st: Rather, the relevant issue is whether it has a crop equivalent to the measure of seeds for dropping in a field in order to sow it.

mishnayos.summary: If locusts or a bad wind ruined a farmer's crop, he pays less rent only if the whole area was hit. Rabbi Yehuda says if he pays rent in money, he never pays less.

chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend
chunks.st: In the case of one who receives a field from another to cultivate

chunks.en: and locusts ate it or it was burnt by wind,
chunks.st: and grasshoppers consumed it or it was wind blasted,

chunks.en: if it is a plague of the whole area,
chunks.st: if it is a regional disaster which affected all the fields in the area,

chunks.en: he takes it off his rent.
chunks.st: the cultivator subtracts from the produce he owes as part of his tenancy.

chunks.en: If it is not a plague of the whole area,
chunks.st: If it is not a regional disaster,

chunks.en: he does not take it off his rent.
chunks.st: the cultivator does not subtract from the produce he owes as part of his tenancy.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if he took it for money,
chunks.st: If the cultivator received it from the owner for a fixed sum of money,

chunks.en: either way
chunks.st: whether this way, i.e., there is a regional disaster, or whether that way, i.e., there was no regional disaster,

chunks.en: he does not take it off his rent.
chunks.st: he does not subtract the produce he owes as part of his tenancy.

mishnayos.summary: A farmer who pays rent in wheat gives wheat from the field itself, whether the crop is poor or very good.

chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend
chunks.st: In the case of one who receives a field from another to cultivate

chunks.en: for ten kor of wheat a year,
chunks.st: in return for the payment of ten kor of wheat per year,

chunks.en: and it got sick, he gives him from it.
chunks.st: and its produce was blighted by a crop disease or the like, the cultivator gives the owner the ten kor of wheat from it but does not have to provide him with high quality wheat.

chunks.en: If its wheat was very good,
chunks.st: If the wheat stalks produced by the field were particularly good stalks of wheat,

chunks.en: he may not say to him,
chunks.st: the cultivator may not say to the owner:

chunks.en: "I will buy from the market,"
chunks.st: I will buy regular wheat from the market;

chunks.en: rather he gives him from it.
chunks.st: rather, he gives him from inside the field itself.

mishnayos.summary: A farmer who agreed to plant barley may not plant wheat, which is harder on the land. He may switch to an easier crop, but Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids that too.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend to plant barley,
chunks.st: With regard to one who receives a field from another in order to plant it with barley,

chunks.en: he may not plant wheat.
chunks.explain: Wheat makes the land weaker.
chunks.st: he may not plant it with wheat, as wheat weakens the field more than barley does.

chunks.en: If wheat, he may plant barley;
chunks.st: But if he receives it in order to plant wheat, he may plant it with barley if he wishes,

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids it.
chunks.st: but Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids it.

chunks.en: Grain, he may not plant beans;
chunks.st: Similarly, if he receives it to plant it with grain he may not plant it with legumes, as they weaken the field more than grains do,

chunks.en: beans, he may plant grain;
chunks.st: but if he receives it in order to plant legumes he may plant it with grain,

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids it.
chunks.st: but Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids it.

mishnayos.summary: A farmer who takes a field for only a few years may not plant flax, which weakens the soil, or cut the sycamore branches. If he takes it for seven years, he may.

chunks.en: If someone takes a field from his friend for a few years,
chunks.st: One who receives a field from another to cultivate for a few years, i.e., fewer than seven,

chunks.en: he may not plant flax,
chunks.st: may not plant flax in it, as flax greatly weakens the soil,

chunks.en: and he has no right to the sycamore branches.
chunks.explain: They take many years to grow back.
chunks.st: and if a sycamore tree was growing in the field, he does not have rights to the beams fashioned from the branches of the sycamore
chunks.stMore: tree. Therefore, he may not cut down its branches for his own use, as it takes many years for new ones to grow.

chunks.en: If he took it for seven years,
chunks.st: If he received the field from him for seven years,

chunks.en: in the first year he may plant flax,
chunks.st: in the first year he may plant flax in it,

chunks.en: and he has a right to the sycamore branches.
chunks.st: and he does have rights to the beams fashioned from the branches of the sycamore tree.

mishnayos.summary: If a farmer rents a field for one shemittah cycle, the shemittah year counts. If he rents it for seven years, the shemittah year does not count, and he gets another year.

chunks.en: If someone took a field from his friend
chunks.st: In the case of one who receives a field from another to cultivate

chunks.en: for one shemittah cycle
chunks.explain: Seven years ending with shemittah, when we do not farm.
chunks.st: for one Sabbatical cycle of seven years culminating with the Sabbatical Year

chunks.en: for 700 zuz,
chunks.st: for seven hundred dinars,

chunks.en: the shemittah year is counted.
chunks.st: the Sabbatical Year is included in the tally, despite the fact that he is unable to work the land during that year.

chunks.en: If he took it for seven years
chunks.st: If he received it from him to cultivate for seven years

chunks.en: for 700 zuz,
chunks.st: for seven hundred dinars,

chunks.en: the shemittah year is not counted.
chunks.st: the Sabbatical Year is not included in the number,
chunks.stMore: and he may keep the field for an additional year to take the place of the Sabbatical Year, during which he could not work the land.

mishnayos.summary: A worker must be paid on time: a day worker by the end of that night, a night worker by the end of the next day, and other workers by when they finish.

chunks.en: A day worker can collect all that night.
chunks.explain: The employer has until morning to pay.
chunks.st: A day laborer collects his wages from his employer all night following his work shift.

chunks.en: A night worker can collect all the next day.
chunks.st: A night laborer collects his wages all the following day,

chunks.en: A worker by the hour
chunks.st: while an hourly laborer

chunks.en: collects all the night and all the day.
chunks.st: collects his wages all night and all day.

chunks.en: A worker for a week, for a month,
chunks.st: With regard to a weekly laborer, a monthly laborer,

chunks.en: for a year, or for seven years:
chunks.st: a yearly laborer, or a laborer for a Sabbatical cycle of seven years,

chunks.en: if he finished by day, he collects all that day;
chunks.st: if he left upon the completion of his work in the day, he collects his wages all day;

chunks.he: יָצָא בַלַּיְלָה, גּוֹבֶה כָל הַלַּיְלָה וְכָל הַיּוֹם:
chunks.en: if he finished at night, he collects all that night and the next day.
chunks.st: if he left at night, he collects his wages all night and all day.

mishnayos.summary: One must pay workers, and rent for animals and vessels, on time when they ask for it. The mishnah teaches when a worker can swear and take his pay, and what is different for a ger toshav.

chunks.en: Whether a person's pay,
chunks.st: Whether referring to a person’s wages that he receives

chunks.en: or rent for an animal,
chunks.st: or the renting of an animal

chunks.en: or rent for vessels,
chunks.st: or the renting of utensils,

chunks.en: all come under
chunks.st: are all subject to the prohibition of:

chunks.en: "On his day you shall give him his pay,"
chunks.st: “On the same day you shall give him his wages” (Deuteronomy 24:15),

chunks.en: and under
chunks.st: and are subject to the prohibition of:

chunks.en: "Do not keep a worker's pay
chunks.st: “The wages of a hired laborer shall not remain

chunks.en: with you until morning."
chunks.st: with you all night until the morning” (Leviticus 19:13).

chunks.en: When? When he asked for it.
chunks.st: When does he transgress these prohibitions? He transgresses them when the one owed the money claimed the payment from him.

chunks.en: If he did not ask for it, he does not break the mitzvah.
chunks.st: If he did not claim his payment from him the other does not transgress the prohibitions.

chunks.en: If he sent him to be paid by a storekeeper or a money changer,
chunks.st: If the one who owes the money transferred his payment by leaving instructions with a storekeeper or with a money changer to pay him,

chunks.en: he does not break the mitzvah.
chunks.st: he does not transgress the prohibitions. The mishna discusses other related halakhot:

chunks.en: A worker, in his time, swears and takes his pay.
chunks.explain: If the employer says he already paid him.
chunks.st: If a hired laborer requests payment at the proper time and the employer claims he already paid him, the laborer takes an oath that he did not receive his wages and then takes the wages from the employer.

chunks.en: If his time passed, he does not swear and take.
chunks.st: If the time had passed, he does not take an oath and take the wages.

chunks.en: If there are witnesses that he asked for it,
chunks.st: If there are witnesses who testify that he claimed the money from him at the proper time,

chunks.en: he swears and takes.
chunks.st: he takes an oath and takes the money.

chunks.en: A ger toshav comes under
chunks.explain: A non-Jew who keeps the seven mitzvos of Bnei Noach.
chunks.st: One who hires a gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav]

chunks.en: "On his day you shall give him his pay,"
chunks.st: is subject to the prohibition of: “On the same day you shall give him his wages,”

chunks.en: but not under "Do not keep

chunks.en: a worker's pay with you until morning."
chunks.st: “The wages of a hired laborer shall not remain with you all night until the morning.”

mishnayos.summary: A lender may take a security only through beis din, and may not go into the borrower's house. He must give back what the poor man needs each day, and may not take from a widow or take things used to make food.

chunks.en: If someone lends money to his friend,
chunks.st: With regard to one who lends money to another and the debtor fails to repay it at the end of the term of the loan,

chunks.en: he may take a security only through beis din,
chunks.explain: A security is something kept until the loan is paid.
chunks.st: the creditor may take collateral from him to ensure payment only by means of an agent of the court, not of his own accord.

words.en: he should take a security from him

chunks.en: and he may not go into his house to take his security,
chunks.st: And he may not enter the debtor’s house to take his collateral,

chunks.en: as it says, "Stand outside."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “When you lend your neighbor any manner of loan, you shall not go into his house to take his collateral. You shall stand outside,

chunks.en: If he had two vessels,
chunks.st: If the debtor had two utensils of the same kind,

chunks.en: he takes one and leaves one.
chunks.st: the creditor takes one and leaves the other one in the debtor’s possession.

chunks.en: And he gives back the pillow at night
chunks.st: And in addition, the creditor must return a pillow at night, as the debtor requires it for sleeping,

chunks.en: and the plow by day.
chunks.st: and a plow, which is needed for his daytime work, by day.

chunks.en: And if he died,
chunks.st: If the debtor died,

chunks.st: he is not required to return it to the debtor’s heirs.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: even to the borrower himself he gives it back
chunks.st: Even to the debtor himself he needs to return the collateral each day

chunks.en: only for thirty days,
chunks.st: only until thirty days have passed,

chunks.he: וּמִשְּׁלשִׁים יוֹם וּלְהַלָּן מוֹכְרָן בְּבֵית דִּין.
chunks.en: and after thirty days he sells them through beis din.
chunks.st: and from thirty days onward, the creditor can sell them in court, with the proceeds going toward payment of the debt.

chunks.he: אַלְמָנָה, בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲנִיָּה בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲשִׁירָה,
chunks.en: A widow, whether she is poor or rich,
chunks.st: With regard to a widow, whether she is poor or whether she is wealthy,

chunks.en: we may not take a security from her,
chunks.st: one may not take collateral from her,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Do not take a widow's garment as a security."
chunks.st: “And you may not take the garment of a widow as collateral” (Deuteronomy 24:17).

chunks.st: One who takes a millstone as collateral

mishnayos.summary: When a house and the floor above it, owned by two people, fall down, the owners share the wood, stones and earth. Whoever recognizes some of his own stones takes them as part of his share.

chunks.st: If one of them

chunks.st: recognized some of his stones

chunks.st: he may take them for himself, and they count toward his amount
chunks.stMore: of stones, and the other party takes other stones accordingly. They do not divide the remaining stones equally.

mishnayos.summary: If the upper floor that someone rents breaks and the owner will not fix it, the renter may live downstairs until it is fixed. Rabbi Yosei teaches who pays for which part of a broken ceiling.

chunks.en: A house and an upper floor of two people:
chunks.st: If there was a house and an upper story owned by one person, and the upper story was rented out to another,

chunks.en: the upper floor broke,
chunks.st: if the floor of the upper story was broken, i.e., it fell in or collapsed,

chunks.en: and the owner of the house does not want to fix it,
chunks.st: and the owner of the house does not want to repair it,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי בַעַל הָעֲלִיָּה יוֹרֵד וְדָר לְמַטָּה,
chunks.en: the one upstairs goes down and lives below
chunks.st: the resident of the upper story can go down and live in the house below

chunks.en: until he fixes the upper floor for him.
chunks.st: until the owner repairs the upper story for him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.stMore: With regard to a house of two stories owned by two people, i.e., the lower level was owned by one and the upper level by the other, in which the ceiling collapsed;

chunks.en: the one below gives the ceiling,
chunks.explain: The beams that hold up the floor.
chunks.st: the owner of the lower story provides the ceiling of beams or stones,

chunks.en: and the one above gives the plaster.
chunks.st: and the owner of the upper story provides the plaster.

mishnayos.summary: When a two-story house owned by two people falls and the lower owner will not rebuild, the upper owner may rebuild and live there until he is paid back. Rabbi Yehuda says he must build both floors so he is not living for free.

chunks.en: If a house and its upper floor, owned by two people, fell down,
chunks.st: In the case of the house and the upper story belonging to two different people, and that house and upper story collapsed,

chunks.he: אָמַר בַּעַל הָעֲלִיָּה לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת לִבְנוֹת,
chunks.en: and the upper owner told the house owner to build,
chunks.st: and the owner of the upper story told the owner of the house to build the lower story in order to enable him to rebuild the upper story,

chunks.en: and he does not want to build,
chunks.st: and he does not want to build it,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי בַעַל הָעֲלִיָּה בּוֹנֶה אֶת הַבַּיִת
chunks.en: the upper owner may build the house
chunks.st: the owner of the upper story may build the house

chunks.en: and live in it
chunks.st: and reside in it,

chunks.en: until he pays him back what he spent.
chunks.st: until the other gives him his expenses
chunks.stMore: for the construction of the house, and he then rebuilds his upper story.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אַף זֶה דָּר בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: "But then he lives in his friend's place,
chunks.st: This one too, i.e., the owner of the upper story, who is meanwhile residing inside the property of the other,

chunks.en: and he would have to pay him rent.
chunks.st: must pay him rent.
chunks.stMore: Since he derived benefit by living in the house of the other, as he had no other place in which he could live, he must pay rent. This solution is therefore flawed.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא בַעַל הָעֲלִיָּה בּוֹנֶה אֶת הַבַּיִת
chunks.en: Rather, the upper owner builds the house
chunks.st: Rather, the owner of the upper story builds the house

chunks.en: and the upper floor, and puts the roof on the upper floor,
chunks.st: and the upper story, and he roofs the upper story, i.e., he completes the entire construction of the upper story,

chunks.en: and lives in the house
chunks.st: and he may then sit in the house, i.e., the lower story,

chunks.en: until he pays him back what he spent."
chunks.explain: He could live upstairs, so living below is not a gain for him.
chunks.st: until the other gives him his expenses
chunks.stMore: for the building of the house, at which point he returns to his upper story. Since in any event he could have lived in the upper story, he is not considered to have derived any benefit by living in the lower story, and is not obligated to pay rent.

mishnayos.summary: If a garden on the roof of an olive press falls in, the garden owner may plant below until the roof is fixed. An owner does not pay for damage from a falling wall or tree unless beis din told him to take it down and he waited too long.

chunks.he: וְכֵן בֵּית הַבַּד שֶׁהוּא בָנוּי בְּסֶלַע,
chunks.en: And the same with an olive press built in a rock,
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of an olive press that is built inside a cave in a rock,

chunks.en: with a garden on top of it,
chunks.st: and one garden, belonging to another person, was planted on top of it,

chunks.he: וְנִפְחַת, הֲרֵי בַעַל הַגִּנָּה יוֹרֵד וְזוֹרֵעַ לְמַטָּה
chunks.en: and it broke through, the garden owner goes down and plants below
chunks.st: and the roof of the olive press broke, which caused the garden to collapse inward, in such a case, the owner of the garden may descend and sow below

chunks.en: until the other makes arches for his olive press.
chunks.explain: Strong arches to hold up the roof.
chunks.st: until the other one constructs for his olive press sturdy arches
chunks.stMore: to support the roof, so that the owner of the garden can once again sow above him. The mishna continues:

chunks.he: הַכֹּתֶל וְהָאִילָן שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְהִזִּיקוּ,
chunks.en: A wall or a tree that fell into a public place and did damage,
chunks.st: In the case of a wall or a tree that fell into the public domain and caused damage,

chunks.en: he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: the owner is exempt from having to pay, as it was an accident.

chunks.en: If they gave him time
chunks.st: If the court saw that the wall was shaky, or that the tree was tilting, and they gave him time

chunks.he: לָקֹץ אֶת הָאִילָן וְלִסְתֹּר אֶת הַכֹּתֶל,
chunks.en: to cut down the tree or knock down the wall,
chunks.st: to cut down the tree or to dismantle the wall,

chunks.en: and they fell within the time, he does not pay;
chunks.st: and then they fell down, if this occurred during the allotted time, he is exempt,

chunks.en: after the time, he must pay.
chunks.st: but if they collapsed after the time given to him had elapsed, he is liable to pay, since he was warned against this very occurrence.

mishnayos.summary: Once someone takes on stones or straw instead of his pay, the other cannot take it back. Things like manure, clay and building stones may stay in a public place only a short time, and whoever leaves them there pays for damage.

chunks.en: If someone's wall was next to
chunks.st: In the case of one whose wall was adjacent to another’s garden,

chunks.en: his friend's garden and it fell,
chunks.st: and the wall fell,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "Clear away your stones,"
chunks.st: and the owner of the garden said to him: Clear away your stones,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "They are yours now,"
chunks.st: and the owner of the stones said to him: They are yours,
chunks.stMore: as I hereby declare them ownerless, and you can take them for yourself;

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
chunks.explain: He cannot force the other to take them.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to him, since he cannot force the other to acquire the stones.

chunks.en: Once the garden owner took them,
chunks.st: If after the owner of the garden voluntarily accepted ownership of the stones upon himself,

chunks.en: if he says to him, "Here are your costs,
chunks.st: the owner of the wall said to him: Here you are, take your expenditures for the removal of the stones,

chunks.en: and I will take mine,"
chunks.st: and I will take the stones that are mine;

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to him,
chunks.stMore: as they had already been acquired by the owner of the garden. The mishna continues:

chunks.en: If someone hires a worker
chunks.st: In the case of one who hires a laborer

chunks.en: to work with him with hay and straw,
chunks.st: to do work with him with hay or with straw, and after he finished the task,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "Give me my pay,"
chunks.st: the laborer said to the employer: Give me my wages, and

chunks.he: וְאָמַר לוֹ טֹל מַה שֶּׁעָשִׂיתָ בִּשְׂכָרֶךָ,
chunks.en: and he said to him, "Take what you worked on as your pay,"
chunks.st: the employer said to him: Take what you have worked with as your wages, i.e., take some of the hay or straw as payment,

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
chunks.explain: He must pay what they agreed.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to him.
chunks.stMore: Although debts can be paid with any item of value, even hay or straw, the wages of a laborer must be paid in accordance with the initial agreement between the laborer and the employer.

chunks.en: Once the worker agreed,
chunks.st: But if after the laborer accepted upon himself to keep the hay or straw as payment, the employer changed his mind

chunks.en: if he says to him, "Here is your pay,
chunks.st: and said to him: Here you are, take your wages

chunks.en: and I will take mine,"
chunks.st: and I will take what is mine;

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to him, since the laborer had already acquired the hay.

chunks.en: If someone takes manure out to a public place,
chunks.st: In the case of one who takes manure out to the public domain, in order for it to be transported to fertilize a field,

chunks.en: the one who takes it out does so, and the one who spreads it does so right away.
chunks.explain: It may not sit in the street.
chunks.st: he who takes it out from his property takes it out, and immediately, he who takes it to fertilize the field takes it to fertilize
chunks.stMore: the field. They must relocate the manure immediately without allowing it to sit around in the public domain.

chunks.en: We may not soak clay in a public place,
chunks.st: Similarly, one may not soak clay in the public domain before it is kneaded,

chunks.en: and we may not make bricks there.
chunks.explain: These take a long time.
chunks.st: and one may not mold bricks
chunks.stMore: in the public domain since this takes a long time and inhibits use of the public domain by others.

chunks.en: But we may knead clay in a public place,
chunks.st: But one may knead clay in the public domain, as this process does not take long,

chunks.en: but not bricks.
chunks.st: but not bricks.

chunks.en: One who builds in a public place:
chunks.st: With regard to one who builds a structure, keeping the building materials in the public domain,

chunks.en: the one who brings stones brings them, and the builder builds right away.
chunks.st: he who brings the stones brings them, and immediately, he who builds the structure builds with them, and may not leave them there.

chunks.en: And if it did damage,
chunks.st: And if the stones cause damage before he had a chance to build them into the structure,

chunks.en: he pays for the damage.
chunks.st: he must pay for what he damaged.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: he may even get his work ready
chunks.st: One may even prepare his work

chunks.en: thirty days before.
chunks.st: thirty days beforehand;
chunks.stMore: he may keep the building materials in the public domain for that duration.

mishnayos.summary: Vegetables grew in the wall of earth between an upper garden and a lower garden. Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon argue about who owns them.

chunks.he: שְׁתֵּי גִנּוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ
chunks.en: Two gardens, one above the other,
chunks.st: In the case of two gardens that were located one above the other, i.e., a garden on a plateau that borders another garden below,

chunks.en: and vegetables in between.
chunks.explain: They grew out of the wall of earth between them.
chunks.st: and vegetables grew in-between,
chunks.stMore: out of the wall of soil resulting from the difference in height between the two gardens,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: they belong to the upper one.
chunks.st: These vegetables belong to the owner of the upper garden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: they belong to the lower one.
chunks.st: They belong to the owner of the lower one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said in explanation of his ruling:

chunks.he: אִם יִרְצֶה הָעֶלְיוֹן לִקַּח אֶת עֲפָרוֹ
chunks.en: "If the upper one wants to take away his earth,
chunks.st: If the owner of the upper garden would want to dig and take his dirt and does so,

chunks.en: there are no vegetables here."
chunks.st: no vegetables would grow here,
chunks.stMore: as that wall made of soil would not exist. The vegetables therefore belong to him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: In response, Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.he: אִם יִרְצֶה הַתַּחְתּוֹן לְמַלְּאוֹת אֶת גִּנָּתוֹ
chunks.en: "If the lower one wants to fill his garden,
chunks.st: If the owner of the lower garden would want to fill his garden with dirt and does so, thereby raising its level,

chunks.en: there are no vegetables here."
chunks.st: no vegetables would grow here,
chunks.stMore: as that wall made of soil would not exist. The vegetables therefore belong to him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:

chunks.en: "Since both of them can stop
chunks.st: Since the two of them can object

chunks.en: each other,
chunks.st: to each other,
chunks.stMore: as they each have the ability to prevent the vegetable growth, nothing can be decided based on such considerations.

chunks.en: we look at where these vegetables get their life from."
chunks.st: Instead, the court considers from where this vegetable lives and derives nourishment, whether from above or from below.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: "Whatever the upper one can reach out
chunks.st: Any vegetables that the owner of the upper garden

chunks.en: his hand and take
chunks.st: can stretch out his hand and take,

chunks.en: is his,
chunks.st: those vegetables are his,

chunks.en: and the rest belongs to the lower one."
chunks.st: and the rest belong to the owner of the lower garden.
